Article Title: A New York mother imprisoned after taking her child without the father's consent faced child-support arrears; an appeals court ordered a fresh review of whether the debt should be capped at $500
Article Text:
The father argued that Chelsea had not explained why she waited so long to seek a change in payments.

Why Chelsea sought a $500 limit

Why the appeals court disagreed

A New York woman jailed for kidnapping her own child has been given another chance to challenge the child-support payments she owes.According to the case details available on Justia , Chelsea Four-Rosenbaum is serving a seven-year prison sentence after taking her child from the family home and keeping the child's whereabouts hidden from the father and police for nearly two months.While in prison, she asked the court to limit her unpaid child-support debt to $500, arguing that her income was too low. On Thursday, a New York appeals court found that the lower court had not properly considered her argument and ordered a fresh hearing. The court now must first find out whether her income during imprisonment was low enough for the limit to apply.Her original child-support payments had been calculated using her earnings before she went to prison, even though she was already behind bars when the order was issued.Chelsea and her husband, Alexander Four-Rosenbaum, have a child born in 2019. Their dispute took a serious turn in 2021, when Chelsea and the child's maternal grandmother took the child from the family home. They kept the child's whereabouts hidden from Alexander and the police for nearly two months. Chelsea was arrested and charged with second-degree kidnapping and endangering the welfare of a child.After her arrest, Alexander filed for divorce and separately sought child support.In 2022, a Family Court ordered Chelsea to pay $408.06 every week towards their child's expenses. The amount was based on her income in 2020, before she was imprisoned.Chelsea was later found guilty of both criminal charges following a jury trial. She received a seven-year prison sentence, followed by five years of supervision after her release.In 2023, Chelsea returned to court seeking changes to her child-support payments. She argued that she had little income while in prison and could not afford the amount she had originally been ordered to pay.She asked for her future payments to be reduced and also argued that the unpaid amount from previous months should be limited to $500 because her income had remained below the federal poverty guidelines.Under Section 413(1)(g) of the Family Court Act, unpaid child support above $500 cannot build up during periods when a parent's income is at or below the federal poverty guidelines for a single person.Chelsea also pointed out that Alexander had started the child-support case only after she was arrested.Alexander argued that Chelsea had not given a good reason for waiting so long before asking the court to change the amount she owed.In February 2024, the Sullivan County Supreme Court partly agreed with Chelsea. It reduced her future child-support payments to $25 per month, the minimum amount required under the law. However, it refused to limit her existing unpaid payments to $500, saying she had not adequately explained why she waited before seeking relief.Chelsea challenged the refusal, bringing the dispute before New York's Appellate Division, Third Department. The appeals court found that the lower court had focused on the wrong question. It had treated Chelsea's request as an attempt to cancel child-support payments that she already owed. Under one provision of New York law, courts generally cannot reduce such debt unless the parent can explain why they did not apply for relief earlier.The earlier decision had also considered Chelsea's past work as a litigation attorney, the circumstances of her imprisonment and whether she might receive money or property through the divorce proceedings. The appeals court found that these issues did not answer whether her income qualified her for the $500 limit.Also, although the lower court had accepted that Chelsea's income was below the poverty level when reducing her future payments, it had not established exactly when her income fell below that level or how long it remained there. The $500 limit may apply only to the periods when her income met the conditions set by law.The appeals court has now sent the case back to the Sullivan County Supreme Court. The court must examine Chelsea's income during the months when the unpaid payments accumulated and decide whether the amount needs to be calculated again.
Article Summary: Chelsea Four-Rosenbaum is serving a seven-year prison sentence after taking her child from the family home and keeping the child's whereabouts hidden from the father and police for nearly two months. While in prison, she asked the court to limit her unpaid child-support debt to $500, arguing that her income was too low. A New York appeals court found that the lower court had not properly considered her argument and ordered a fresh hearing.

Article Title: After 47 years of marriage, a Kentucky couple divorced but disagreed over selling their jointly owned $703,000 farm; an October 23 appeals court overturned the ruling favouring the husband and ordered
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI-generated)

Divorce agreement left the farm’s future uncertain

Wife sought sale after their son moved out

Appeals court finds agreement ambiguous

Case returns for a fresh review

A divorce settlement intended to divide a couple’s property has led to a fresh legal battle over a $703,000 Kentucky farm. After nearly 47 years of marriage, Mary Holden and Fred Holden agreed to retain equal ownership of the property, but disagreed over when it should be sold. According to the Kentucky Court of Appeals’ October 23, 2026, opinion in Mary Holden (now Carrigan) v. Fred Holden, available on Justia , the court overturned a lower court ruling that favoured Fred’s interpretation of the agreement. The case has been sent back to the family court to determine what the former spouses originally intended.Mary and Fred Holden married in 1972 and divorced after approximately 47 years together. In February 2021, they entered into a property settlement agreement that was incorporated into their divorce decree. The agreement covered their jointly owned farm at 3100 Apple Hill Road in Louisville, Kentucky, valued at $703,000. Both former spouses retained 50% ownership interests, with rights of survivorship.The settlement prohibited either party from selling, transferring, renting, mortgaging or otherwise encumbering their interest without the other’s express written consent.It also stated that Fred could continue using the farm, its equipment and tools to raise crops for “at least the next two years, after which the property will be listed for sale.” The net proceeds from the eventual sale were to be divided equally. The disagreement centred on whether the property had to be listed after two years or whether Fred could continue farming indefinitely, delaying the sale for as long as he used the land for agricultural purposes.According to the court opinion, the couple’s son moved out of the farm residence in January 2024. Mary subsequently asked Fred either to purchase her share or agree to list the property for sale. Fred offered $125,000 for her interest. Mary rejected the offer, pointing to an earlier appraisal that valued the farm at substantially more than twice that amount. Fred later declined to negotiate further or agree to put the property on the market.On March 25, 2025, Mary filed a motion asking the Jefferson Family Court to order the farm listed for sale. The following month, she sought summary judgment, arguing that the settlement clearly required the property to be listed after the initial two-year period. Fred disagreed, maintaining that the wording allowed him to continue farming beyond that period. On September 3, 2025, the family court sided with him, concluding that he could continue using the property for as long as he farmed it. The court denied Mary’s request to order a sale, prompting her appeal.The Kentucky Court of Appeals examined whether the disputed provision was unambiguous, reviewing that legal question independently. It concluded that both parties had reasonable interpretations of the wording. Mary argued that the agreement guaranteed Fred at least two years of farming but separately required the property to be listed for sale after that period. Under her interpretation, he could continue farming while the property was marketed and until a sale was completed.Fred relied on the words “at least” to argue that his right to use the farm extended beyond two years. He also pointed to provisions requiring both parties to share property taxes and insurance in subsequent years, which he said supported continued joint ownership and farming. The appeals court acknowledged that “at least” did not establish a strict two-year limit on Fred’s use. However, that did not automatically mean continued farming could postpone the sale indefinitely.Because the agreement did not expressly explain whether ongoing agricultural use would delay listing the property, the judges found the provision ambiguous. They therefore rejected the lower court’s conclusion that the written agreement conclusively supported Fred’s interpretation.The appeals court vacated the September 3, 2025, order and sent the dispute back to the Jefferson Family Court for further proceedings. It did not order an immediate sale. The lower court can now consider evidence beyond the written agreement, including the circumstances surrounding its execution, the former spouses’ intentions and their conduct after signing it.That evidence will help determine whether Fred’s continued farming was meant to postpone the sale or whether the property was supposed to be listed after two years regardless of his agricultural use. The ruling leaves the farm’s future unresolved. It highlights how unclear wording in divorce settlements can lead to prolonged disputes, even when ownership shares and the division of sale proceeds are explicitly established.
Article Summary: Mary and Fred Holden married in 1972 and divorced after approximately 47 years together. In February 2021, they entered into a property settlement agreement that was incorporated into their divorce decree. The agreement covered their jointly owned farm at 3100 Apple Hill Road in Louisville, Kentucky, valued at $703,000. Both former spouses retained 50% ownership interests, with rights of survivorship. The disagreement centred on whether the property had to be listed after two years or whether Fred could continue farming indefinitely.

Article Title: ‘We got them both’: Donald Trump claims US has secured Greenland, Venezuela in ‘greatest real estate deal’
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump speaks at a campaign rally at Guardian Centers of Georgia, in Perry, Georgia (AP photo)

US-Denmark agreement does not cover Greenland

Trump highlights Greenland's strategic and energy potential

Venezuela claims follow Maduro's capture

Trump announces Audi investment at Georgia rally

US President Donald Trump has claimed that the United States has secured control over Greenland and Venezuela, describing the purported acquisitions as the “greatest real estate deal in history” during a campaign rally for Republican candidates in Perry, Georgia, on Saturday (local time).However, neither territory has been transferred to US sovereignty.Addressing supporters, Trump claimed Denmark had handed Greenland over to Washington and boasted of US dominance over Venezuela and its oil reserves.“Denmark was so great, they gave us Greenland. You do know that, right? We already have that. We're doing good with that, aren't we?” Trump told the crowd.He also referred to earlier concerns that the US would attempt to take control of the Arctic island.“All of them talked, 'Donald Trump, Donald Trump, he's going to attack! He's going to attack Greenland!' But Denmark gave us—we signed an agreement. You know what? The press hardly covered it. It's going to go down as the greatest real estate deal in history, probably after Venezuela. I think Venezuela. What do you take: Venezuela or Greenland? Both? We got them both!” he said.Trump's remarks came days after the United States and Denmark signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on October 22 to strengthen maritime industrial cooperation and expand US shipbuilding capabilities.However, the agreement explicitly excludes Greenland and the Faroe Islands. Its section on legal status and scope states: “This MoU does not apply to Greenland or the Faroe Islands.”The document also clarifies that it records political intentions rather than constituting an international treaty.It creates no legal rights or obligations and “does not authorise any procurement, award of contracts or transfer of funds between the Participants”. Each country is expected to bear its own costs.Denmark has not transferred sovereignty over Greenland. Although a defence agreement expanded US military rights in the region, it continues to recognise Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination.Denmark's ministry of foreign affairs highlighted the commercial focus of the maritime agreement in a statement on X, quoting foreign minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen.“Today, Denmark signs an agreement with the US, which paves the way for Danish expertise and solutions in US maritime efforts. The agreement opens significant opportunities for Danish companies and can create new jobs on both sides of the Atlantic,” Rasmussen said.The framework covers three areas: education and training to strengthen the US maritime workforce; equipment, technology and services to modernise shipbuilding, repair and retrofit capabilities; and defence industrial cooperation involving technologies with both civilian and military applications. Commercial contracts are to be finalised separately.The president's claims follow a series of US moves concerning Greenland, an Arctic territory that remains under Danish sovereignty.On October 13, Trump announced on Truth Social that large-scale oil, gas and mineral exploration was preparing to begin in Greenland.The announcement followed a tripartite agreement reached the previous month involving Washington, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen to strengthen Arctic security and defence cooperation.“Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland!” Trump wrote, adding that the territory's resources and strategic location were important to US and European security.He also argued that Greenland's position would help the United States detect and counter potential threats, including drones and missiles.Trump's assertion that the United States had also secured Venezuela came after major political and military developments in the South American country earlier this year.In January, US forces carried out an operation that captured former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. The couple was detained, transferred to a US naval vessel and flown to New York to face criminal indictments.The operation prompted scrutiny from international legal scholars over potential violations of Venezuelan sovereignty. Trump defended the action, saying the United States had liberated Venezuela from a “very powerful, very nasty dictatorship”.In September, Venezuela's Acting President Delcy Rodríguez addressed the United Nations General Assembly for the first time and signalled a diplomatic reset. She said Venezuela would take “historic responsibility” for guiding the country towards democratic elections and full democracy on its own timeline.Rodríguez also expressed a desire to rebuild relations with Washington.“Venezuela aspires—with the United States, with its neighbours, and with all the countries of our continent and the international community—to rebuild and sustain relations based on cooperation, respect, and equality,” she said.She added that Venezuela was seeking a national “rebirth” after a period marked by internal political tensions, heightened military confrontation with Washington and earthquakes on June 24.Trump's remarks on Greenland and Venezuela came at a rally where he also announced plans for a major automobile manufacturing investment in Georgia.The president said German luxury carmaker Audi, owned by Volkswagen, would invest $4.2 billion in a plant near Macon capable of producing 200,000 vehicles annually.He credited his tariff policies for the decision.Audi chairman Gernot Döllner, who appeared alongside Trump, said the facility would manufacture “our biggest and most premium SUVs”.“This is a long-term investment, because we believe in the American market,” Döllner said.According to Audi's announcement, the plant is expected to create approximately 4,500 jobs, with construction scheduled to begin in 2027 and production planned for the early 2030s.The rally was held as Republicans seek to retain their majorities in Congress ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Trump has spent October campaigning in Republican-leaning states as the party faces concerns over the president's unpopularity, high living costs and the ongoing war in Iran.Rick Jackson, the Republican candidate for Georgia governor, welcomed the investment announcement, saying: “Thank you on behalf of Georgia for putting the biggest economic deal in Georgia history right here today.”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has claimed that the United States has secured control over Greenland and Venezuela. He described the purported acquisitions as the ‘greatest real estate deal in history’ However, neither territory has been transferred to US sovereignty. The president's claims follow a series of US moves concerning Greenland.

Article Title: Europe Spring? Protests engulf continent as people take to streets in France, Albania, Italy, Spain, Portugal
Article Text:
Protests sweep Europe as thousands take to streets across countries

France sees arrests as protests turn violent

Albania protests see clashes with riot police

Italy deploys soldiers amid renewed demonstrations

Spain rallies focus on pensions and housing

Lisbon housing protest camp cleared by police

Thousands of people took to the streets across Europe over the weekend to protest against rising living costs, housing affordability, pensions, education standards, alleged corruption and war, with demonstrations in several countries leading to clashes with police and tighter security measures.France, Albania, Italy, Spain and Portugal witnessed rallies on Saturday, with demonstrators raising demands ranging from action against government corruption and investment in education to protection of public pensions and access to affordable housing.Authorities deployed additional police personnel and, in some areas, soldiers after violence during earlier demonstrations. While several rallies remained peaceful, others saw protesters throw projectiles at police, set fires and damage property.In France, nearly 1,000 people had been arrested during Saturday's demonstrations, interior minister Laurent Nuñez said, adding that the figure was likely to rise further.The government estimated that 410,000 people had taken part in protests nationwide, while organisers put the turnout at nearly 800,000.Authorities in Paris announced that the demonstration along Cours de Vincennes had been dispersed following clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel, France 24 reported.Police used water cannons and tear gas after projectiles were thrown at officers."A Gendarmerie helicopter has been deployed to support ground units and locate any remaining groups of rioters," the prefectural police said, adding that more than 500 people described as rioters had been present towards the end of the demonstration.French left-wing leader and presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon criticised the police response, accusing officers of using tear gas and firing into the crowd at the back of the procession. He also alleged that media coverage was presenting the protest movement negatively.US President Donald Trump also commented on the unrest during a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia, on Saturday, blaming France's immigration policies for the situation.In Albania, thousands of people gathered in the capital, Tirana, for another anti-government demonstration, with protests also spreading to other cities.Riot police used tear gas, water cannons and rubber bullets to disperse demonstrators who threw rocks at officers and started a fire at the entrance to the agriculture ministry, Reuters reported.Visuals showed protesters firing streams of firework rockets towards riot police and fireworks exploding.Protesters also targeted government buildings and banks, smashed shop windows and pulled up paving stones to throw at police.The student-led demonstrations have been fuelled by anger over alleged government corruption, unemployment and poor education standards.High school and university students have demanded lower tuition fees, greater state investment in education and action against corruption in the education system. Some have joined a wider movement calling for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.The unrest follows months of largely peaceful summer protests against a luxury coastal development backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.Authorities deployed around 2,500 police officers in Tirana on Saturday. Protesters had hurled rocks, flares, firebombs and fireworks at police over the preceding week, while authorities said more than 300 protesters and police personnel had been injured.Thousands of young people marched in Milan, Rome, Turin, Naples, Bologna and Florence, with demonstrations focusing on a range of social and political concerns. Some protesters threw bottles, stones and firecrackers.Italian police said nine people had been arrested and 371 briefly detained during demonstrations in eight cities on Saturday. Of those taken to police stations, 110 were minors.In Milan, the march remained peaceful as authorities deployed soldiers and police personnel and several luxury shops boarded up their windows. Most shops had reopened by late afternoon.Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced that an additional 500 soldiers would be sent to Milan, alongside tougher penalties for minors involved in violence. Hundreds of soldiers were already stationed in the city, supporting around 5,000 police and other security personnel.Meloni thanked law enforcement personnel for protecting public safety and the right to peaceful protest."The right to demonstrate must always be guaranteed, just as the right of citizens to live their cities in safety must be," she wrote in a post on X.In Rome, a small group of protesters tried to force their way into the Colosseum but were ushered out by guards.A separate anti-war march briefly clashed with police near Piazza della Repubblica, with demonstrators retreating after officers deployed a water cannon, news agency AP reported.The latest demonstrations followed violent clashes and looting during protests the previous weekend. In Milan, shops in the fashion district, including luxury boutiques, had boarded up their windows in anticipation of renewed unrest.In Madrid, thousands of retirees and other demonstrators marched to demand protection for the public pension system and increases linked to actual inflation.Protesters called for higher minimum pensions in line with the minimum wage, measures to narrow the gender pension gap and safeguards against the privatisation of public pensions.As per reports, thereChaos on the streets was captured in several viral videos on social media.The demonstrations came ahead of a snap election next month. Spain's governing Socialist Party has criticised the conservative opposition Popular Party over proposals it says could open the door to privatising public pensions.Housing affordability has also been a source of discontent in Spain, where rental and home prices have risen in recent years beyond what many people can afford.In Portugal, affordable housing was a central demand as thousands marched through Lisbon on Saturday. Protesters opposed rising rents and living costs, arguing that housing had become increasingly difficult to afford, particularly for younger people.After the march, demonstrators pitched more than 100 tents in Rossio Square. Police moved in shortly after 2 am on Sunday to clear the encampment, charging protesters and making several arrests. Minor injuries were reported, although figures were not immediately available, Reuters reported.Hundreds had gathered at the site to protect the camp after police dismantled a similar encampment on Tuesday."We have an obligation to fight for what we believe in," said Vitor Gomes, a 21-year-old multimedia communications student, citing housing speculation, concentrated wealth and rising inequality as reasons for his pessimism about the future.Protesters called on the government to scrap a bill that would make evictions easier and remove rent caps on new leases. The legislation had passed its first parliamentary reading, Reuters reported.Portugal is facing a severe housing affordability crisis, with house prices more than doubling since 2017 and rents for new leases nearly doubling over the same period. The Bank of Portugal estimates that the country faces a shortfall of 300,000 homes.The protests across Europe reflected a broad range of demands, from education and corruption to pensions and housing, while clashes in several cities prompted authorities to strengthen security and step up efforts to prevent further violence.
Article Summary: France, Albania, Italy, Spain and Portugal witnessed rallies on Saturday. Demonstrations in several countries saw clashes with police and tighter security measures. In France, nearly 1,000 people had been arrested during Saturday's demonstrations, interior minister Laurent Nuñez said.

Article Title: Kansas woman says she agreed to buy her cousin’s home on about 5 acres after curing a $9,055 mortgage default; four years later he received a $150,000 offer, but an appeals court enforced their oral d
Article Text:
The dispute escalated in March 2024 when Miller spotted a sale sign outside the property. (AI image)

How a mortgage problem led to the agreement

Years of repairs became important to the case

Why court rejected Harvey's appeal

A Kansas man who received a $150,000 offer for his property has lost a legal battle with his cousin, who claimed he had already agreed to sell her the house and about five acres of land four years earlier. Tiffany Miller said she took responsibility for the property in 2020 after discovering that her cousin, Aaron Harvey, had fallen behind on mortgage payments. Although they never signed a sale agreement, the Kansas Court of Appeals ruled on Friday that their verbal arrangement could be enforced.The dispute began when Harvey decided to sell the property in 2024. By then, Miller and her son had been paying the mortgage and looking after the house for several years. They had also spent money repairing the building and improving the surrounding land. Harvey, however, maintained that he had never agreed to sell it to them.According to the court ruling available on Justia , the disagreement came to a head in March 2024, when Miller noticed a sale sign outside the Kansas City property. Harvey later told the court that he had received a $150,000 offer from another buyer, who had also provided a cashier's cheque.At the time of the trial, around $49,000 remained outstanding on the mortgage.Harvey had owned the property since 2004. He had previously lived there and borrowed $75,000 in 2005 to renovate the house and build an arena for cattle roping. Miller was familiar with the land because her son, Demetre, kept horses there.In January 2020, while visiting to feed the horses, Miller came across a letter addressed to Harvey. She testified that it warned the property was at risk of foreclosure and that $9,055.68 was needed to bring the mortgage payments up to date.Miller contacted Harvey about the letter and said he indicated that he no longer wanted the property. She then offered to buy it.According to Miller, they agreed on a price of $80,000. With approximately $61,000 still owed on the mortgage, she would take responsibility for the loan and pay Harvey the remaining $19,000 by January 1, 2025. He would then transfer ownership to her.The overdue mortgage amount was not paid as a single upfront payment. Instead, Miller arranged a modification of the loan, which added the overdue amount to the mortgage balance. The lender approved the arrangement in May 2020.Harvey gave a different account. He said he had simply allowed Miller's family to use the property in exchange for paying the mortgage and utility bills. He denied agreeing to sell it.The condition of the house became an important part of the dispute. Miller testified that when she first received the keys in January 2020, she found mud, mould and mildew in the basement, along with a sewer smell. When she told Harvey about the problems, she said he responded, "That's your deal now."Miller and her son subsequently carried out extensive work. They repaired plumbing, replaced household appliances, improved fencing and worked on the driveway and cattle arena. They also installed a French drain to prevent water from entering the basement. Her son began contributing towards the mortgage, utilities and repairs after moving into the property in 2022.Harvey argued that he had not been informed about the improvements. However, the trial court found that his actions supported Miller's account, particularly because he had given her access to the mortgage account and allowed her to take possession of the property.Harvey argued that the original arrangement was unfair because the property had subsequently attracted a $150,000 offer. He pointed out that Miller would pay him only $19,000 directly, even though the property's value had increased considerably.The appeals court disagreed with that comparison. The judges explained that the agreed purchase price was $80,000, including the mortgage Miller had undertaken to pay. They also considered the repairs and improvements made over the years.Another issue involved Miller's bankruptcy filing in 2022. She admitted that she had not disclosed the property agreement or mortgage payments, describing the omission as an "honest mistake". Harvey argued that this should prevent her from claiming the property, but the appeals court found that he had not properly raised that defence during the earlier proceedings.The judges also considered whether an agreement that was never written down could still be enforced. Although Kansas law generally requires property-sale agreements to be in writing, exceptions can apply when someone has already acted substantially on an agreement.In this case, the court found sufficient evidence that Miller had acted on the arrangement by taking possession, arranging the mortgage payments and making significant improvements.The judges also concluded that simply paying her back for the repairs would not adequately compensate her for losing the property she had agreed to buy.
Article Summary: Tiffany Miller took responsibility for the property in 2020 after discovering that her cousin, Aaron Harvey, had fallen behind on mortgage payments. The dispute escalated in March 2024 when Miller spotted a sale sign outside the property. Harvey later told the court that he had received a $150,000 offer from another buyer.

Article Title: Kim Jong Un photos released to dismiss rumours of coma, takeover by sister
Article Text:
Kim Jong Un inspects pink shoe, women’s coats as death rumours grip North Korea

How the death rumours began

Claims of Chinese troop deployment

What is known about Kim's health?

North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media, inspecting children's footwear and women's clothing, after unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.The photographs, published by North Korea's official media on Monday, show Kim examining footwear, gesturing towards officials and inspecting coats at a garment and footwear exhibition. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis in the secretive country, the New York Post reported.According to North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency, Kim toured the exhibition on Monday. However, the photographs have not been independently authenticated, and it remains unclear precisely when they were taken.One image shows Kim bending forward to inspect a small pink shoe held by a woman. In another, he gestures with his arms outstretched as he appears to address an official. A third photograph captures him reaching towards the sleeve of a woman's coat displayed on a mannequin.The speculation gathered pace after Wanjun Xie, a US-based Chinese dissident associated with the China Democracy Party, posted a series of claims on X alleging that Kim had died and that his sister, Kim Yo Jong , had taken control of the country.In a post on Monday, Xie wrote: "Rumours of the death of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un have been circulating online for days, but Kim Jong Un has not yet made a public appearance to deny them. This indirectly confirms that the rumours of Kim Jong Un's death are likely true. Furthermore, it is rumoured that after Kim Jong-un's death, the North Korean regime has not been transferred to his daughter Kim Ju-ae, but is currently in the hands of his sister Kim Yo-jong."After assuming power, Kim Yo-jong immediately activated loudspeaker broadcasts to South Korea and fired 201 warning shots. She also warned South Korea that North Korea was considering a comprehensive upgrade of its tactical strike capabilities. This sudden intensification of threats against South Korea is clearly aimed at strengthening her control over the North Korean military and consolidating her power through strong external threats. This indirectly confirms the rumors that Kim Jong-un is dead and that Kim Yo-jong is currently in control of the regime; these rumors are likely true."The New York Post reported that Xie's claims began gaining traction on Sunday. However, the allegations have not been supported by medical records, identifiable witnesses or other independently verifiable evidence.In another post on Sunday, Xie claimed that Kim had suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage, fallen into a coma and been transferred to Beijing for emergency treatment. He alleged that a team of specialists from Peking Union Medical College Hospital had travelled to North Korea before Kim was moved to China."It is rumoured that recently, Kim Jong-un, General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and Supreme Leader of North Korea, suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage and fell into a coma. Although a team of medical experts from Peking Union Medical College Hospital was dispatched to North Korea to assist in his treatment, the poor medical conditions in North Korea forced Kim Jong-un to be transferred to Peking Union Medical College Hospital for emergency treatment. However, due to the severity of his condition and the fact that the optimal window for treatment had passed, Kim Jong-un succumbed to his injuries and died. His body has been secretly transported back to North Korea, and the news of his death is being kept under wraps."Xie further alleged that Kim's body had been secretly returned to North Korea and that authorities were concealing news of his death. He also claimed that Chinese troops had been deployed to Pyongyang amid fears of a succession crisis.In a separate post, he wrote: "It is said that on October 17, Peking Union Medical College Hospital dispatched a team of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular medical experts to North Korea to participate in the rescue of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, who was in critical condition."Xie's posts also fuelled speculation about a possible power struggle involving Kim's daughter, Kim Ju-ae, and his sister, Kim Yo Jong. He claimed that China had sent 9,000 troops to Pyongyang to help stabilise the situation.The claims of Kim's death, a Chinese troop deployment and a possible succession crisis remain unverified. North Korean authorities have not explicitly addressed the death reports.Kim's health has long been the subject of international speculation. The New York Post reported that South Korea's National Intelligence Service told lawmakers on September 30 that Kim weighed approximately 140 kilograms (309 pounds) and faced an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease because of severe obesity.However, the agency reportedly detected no significant signs of ill health, pointing to Kim's ability to run up stairs during an inspection of a naval destroyer.The latest rumours echo a false alarm in 2020, when Ji Seong-ho, a North Korean defector who later became a South Korean lawmaker, claimed he was "99%" certain that Kim had died following cardiovascular surgery. Kim subsequently appeared in public, and Ji apologised for making the erroneous claim.The New York Post said it had sought comment from the governments of North Korea and China, as well as Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
Article Summary: North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis. Unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.

Article Title: Typhoon Champi: Taiwan issues land warning, cancels 125 flights as powerful storm approaches
Article Text:
Nasa's Terra satellite shows Typhoon Noul in the Pacific Ocean, approaching Taiwan and Japan's main islands on its northward journey (Reuters image)

Taiwan issued a land warning for powerful Typhoon Champi on Thursday and cancelled 125 flights as the storm approached the island's northeastern coast, bringing the threat of destructive winds, torrential rain and waves exceeding six metres, Reuters reported.Champi, which was previously classified as a super typhoon, weakened slightly but continued to pack gusts of more than 227 kmph near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration. The storm was about 520 km southeast of Taiwan's southern tip and was expected to pass close to the northeastern coast late on Friday before moving north towards the Chinese coast.Taiwan President Lai Ching-te urged residents to prepare for the storm and avoid mountainous and coastal areas."A little more preparation means less risk," he wrote on his Facebook page.Mobile phone alerts warning of waves exceeding six metres were issued to coastal towns, while rainfall approaching one metre was forecast in northern mountainous areas, including hills near the capital Taipei. Weather experts warned that the storm's impact could last nearly two days.Taiwan's transport ministry said 125 flights had been cancelled on Thursday, mostly domestic services, while the rail network remained unaffected.The interior ministry said no evacuations had been reported.Champi is also forecast to pass over Yonaguni, Japan's westernmost inhabited island in Okinawa Prefecture. Japan Airlines, ANA and Skymark cancelled more than 100 flights between Thursday and Sunday, mostly domestic services, disrupting travel for more than 11,000 passengers.
Article Summary: Taiwan issues land warning for powerful Typhoon Champi. 125 flights cancelled as storm approaches island's northeastern coast. Article Title: Explosion, fuel leak: Two Syrian pipelines damaged in fresh blow to war-hit energy network
Article Text:
Security forces of Syria's Interior Ministry guard the al-Omar oil field, the country's largest by area and production

Two pipelines carrying gas and petroleum products were damaged in separate incidents in Syria on Thursday, with one explosion triggering a fire and another causing a fuel leak, Syrian state media reported.According to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA), citing the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Company, an explosion struck the Jbessa gas pipeline in Hasakah province, while a separate leak was detected on the Baniyas-Homs petroleum-products pipeline near Homs.The explosion struck the Jbessa gas export pipeline in the al-Arabidi area of Hasakah province, setting the pipeline on fire. Emergency teams isolated the damaged section and shut valves to contain the blaze.The Syrian Petroleum Company described the incident as sabotage. Officials said alternative arrangements would maintain gas supplies to power stations during repairs, while domestic gas supplies remained unaffected.In a separate incident, a hole was discovered in the Baniyas-Homs pipeline in the Hadida area west of Homs, causing a leak of petroleum products. Emergency and technical teams were deployed to contain the leak and isolate the damaged section.Al Jazeera, citing Syrian state media, reported that the damage to the Baniyas-Homs pipeline was believed to be linked to an attempted fuel theft. The initial reports did not confirm the cause or identify those responsible.The incidents come amid a series of disruptions to Syria’s energy infrastructure. Earlier in October, an oil pipeline near Tal Hamis in Hasakah province was damaged in what the Syrian Petroleum Company described as sabotage.Syria is working to rebuild its oil and gas infrastructure after years of conflict, restoring production in northeastern oilfields and reconnecting them with processing facilities and refineries in Homs and Baniyas.In January 2026, the Syrian Petroleum Company began pumping raw gas from the Jbessa fields in Hasakah to the Furqlus gas plant in Homs countryside at around 1.2 million cubic metres per day to support electricity generation.The second damaged pipeline, connecting Baniyas on the Mediterranean coast to Homs, transports petroleum products between two important energy centres. The Baniyas refinery is undergoing an overhaul aimed at increasing its processing capacity from around 80,000 to 130,000 barrels per day.Syria has also undertaken emergency pipeline repairs and plans to expand its transportation network. A September 2026 analysis by the Baker Institute for Public Policy reported that the Syrian Petroleum Company was repairing existing infrastructure and planning a heavy-crude pipeline linking northeastern oilfields to the Baniyas refinery.
Article Summary: Two pipelines carrying gas and petroleum products were damaged in separate incidents in Syria on Thursday. One explosion struck the Jbessa gas export pipeline in the al-Arabidi area of Hasakah province, setting the pipeline on fire. Emergency teams isolated the damaged section and shut valves to contain the blaze. A separate leak was detected on the Baniyas-Homs petroleum-products pipeline near Homs.

Article Title: Kylie Jenner launched a lip kit in 2015 and built a global cosmetics brand; Coty agreed to pay $600 million for a 51% stake in 2019
Article Text:
Image: Left/Britannica/Right/Refinery29

How the November 2015 Kylie Lip Kit launch became Kylie Cosmetics, a beauty brand with global reach

Kylie Cosmetics stand at Melbourne Airport, Australia. Image Credit: Wikipedia

Why Coty agreed to pay 600 million dollars for 51 per cent ownership of the Kylie Jenner partnership

Kylie Jenner arrives at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party on Sunday, March 15, 2026, at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art in LA.

177 million dollars in revenue, growth targets and the financial case for Coty

How creative control, licensing and Coty's manufacturing reach shaped the global beauty expansion plan

Where Coty stands today as a global beauty company and how the Kylie Jenner partnership fits its plans

Few beauty stories capture the power of social media as clearly as the rise of Kylie Jenner 's cosmetics business. What began in November 2015 as a debut lip kit became Kylie Cosmetics, a brand that built a devoted audience online and then attracted one of the largest beauty companies in the world. In November 2019, that company, Coty, agreed to buy a majority stake in the business for 600 million dollars. Here’s how the brand grew, what the agreement contained, why the numbers mattered, and how the partnership was designed to carry the business into new global markets. The deal also marked a turning point in the influencer-led beauty industry, demonstrating how a strong digital following could translate into a valuable global consumer brand.Coty's press release describes the origin story plainly. In November 2015, Kylie Jenner launched Kylie Cosmetics, and the debut product, the Kylie Lip Kit, was a sell-out success. Her online store, KylieCosmetics.com, is one of the most successful online stores in the world, and the range grew well beyond lips to include eyeliners, eyeshadows, blushes, highlighters, concealers, brushes and makeup bags, plus limited edition sets released throughout the year.In May 2019, she introduced Kylie Skin, a range of skincare products. The audience behind it was enormous, Coty says she has more than 270 million followers across her personal and brand social media channels, and that both brands are among the fastest-growing and most-engaged beauty brands on social media. Forbes featured her as the youngest-ever self-made billionaire in August 2018.On 18 November 2019, Coty and Kylie Jenner announced a long-term strategic partnership. Under the terms of the agreement, Coty would acquire 51 per cent ownership in the partnership for 600 million dollars, and the acquisition was expected to close in the third quarter of Coty's fiscal year 2020. Coty described the transaction as a key milestone in its ongoing transformation into a more focused and agile company. Chairman of the Board Peter Harf told the public that the partnership was an exciting step in Coty's renewed emphasis on its beauty business, calling Kylie Jenner a modern-day icon with an incredible sense of the beauty consumer. Pierre Laubies, Coty's chief executive officer, told the public the company was pleased to welcome her into its organisation and family.Coty's press release sets out the financial case in specific terms. Kylie Cosmetics generated an estimated 177 million dollars in net revenues over the preceding twelve months. Coty said it expected the transaction to add more than 1 per cent per year to the net revenue growth of its core fragrance, cosmetics and skin care portfolio over the next three years. The company also expected the deal to be neutral to its earnings per share in the first year and to add to them afterwards, and it expected the return on invested capital to exceed its cost of capital by fiscal year 2023. Tiger Shark served as an advisor to Coty on the transaction. Coty also scheduled a conference call that morning, with the live audio webcast and presentation slides made available through its investor relations website.The agreement divides responsibilities along each side's strengths. Together, Coty and Kylie Jenner set and lead the strategic direction, focusing on global expansion and entry into new beauty categories. Kylie Jenner and her team keep leading all creative efforts in product and communications, building on her global reach through social media. Coty takes overall responsibility for developing the portfolio, drawing on its knowledge of research and development, manufacturing, distribution and commercial strategy, and it acts as licensee for skincare, fragrances and nail products. All beauty categories continue to be sold through leading luxury beauty retailers and owned digital channels. Both parties aim to build what Coty calls a high-growth, digitally native beauty brand. Kylie Jenner told the public the partnership lets her team stay focused on creating and developing each product while building an international beauty powerhouse.Coty's own investor relations website shows the scale of the company that Kylie Jenner partnered with. Founded in Paris in 1904, Coty describes itself as one of the world's largest beauty companies, with a portfolio spanning fragrance, colour cosmetics, and skin and body care. The site lists the company as second globally in both fragrances and mass colour cosmetics, with more than 60 brands and licenses, about 11,300 employees, seven manufacturing sites and sales in more than 120 countries. For fiscal 2026, it reports net revenues of 5.8 billion dollars, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of 847 million dollars, and free cash flow of 348 million dollars. Pairing that infrastructure with a creator-led brand is what the partnership set out to do.
Article Summary: Coty and Kylie Jenner announced a long-term strategic partnership. Under the terms of the agreement, Coty would acquire 51 per cent ownership in the partnership for 600 million dollars. The acquisition was expected to close in the third quarter of Coty's fiscal year 2020. Both parties aim to build what Coty calls a high-growth beauty brand.

Article Title: In 2022, a Florida buyer paid a $1.65 million deposit for a $5.5 million luxury condo; four years later, his home remains unfinished as the developer faces a $418 million foreclosure lawsuit
Article Text:
A luxury project that missed its deadlines

Buyers fight to recover million-dollar deposits

A $418 million foreclosure adds to the uncertainty

Could buyers lose their deposits?

In 2022, Florida buyer Nilesh Undavia put down $1.65 million for a luxury condominium that was supposed to be ready by the end of the year. Four years later, the apartment remains unfinished and his deposit has yet to be returned, even after an arbitration ruling in his favour. The case is part of a growing dispute surrounding Boca Raton’s Mandarin Oriental Residences, where buyers are seeking refunds as the developer faces a $417.7 million foreclosure lawsuit, according to reporting by The New York Times, The Real Deal and The Coastal Star. The development, part of the ambitious Via Mizner project in South Florida, was marketed as an upscale destination combining luxury residences, hotel services and resort-style amenities. Instead, years of construction delays, mounting debts and legal disputes have left prospective homeowners uncertain about when, or whether, they will receive the properties they paid for.Penn-Florida Companies unveiled plans for Via Mizner in 2015, proposing a 2.3-million-square-foot development featuring a Mandarin Oriental hotel, branded condominiums, rental apartments and high-end retail and dining spaces.The original completion target was late 2017. The wider development was designed to offer residents access to amenities including a swimming pool, golf facilities, a country club and a wine cellar. Buyers were also paying for the appeal of living in a property associated with the internationally recognised Mandarin Oriental luxury hospitality brand.However, the project has fallen substantially behind schedule. The rental apartments are operational, but the hotel and condominium components have encountered serious financial and construction problems. Penn-Florida has attributed the delays to a combination of the pandemic, hurricanes, rising construction costs, supply-chain disruptions and higher interest rates. The company has said that close to $1 billion has been invested in the wider development.Undavia’s case illustrates the financial risks facing buyers who committed substantial sums to properties that have yet to be completed. He agreed to purchase a four-bedroom condominium for $5.5 million in 2022, paying a deposit of $1.65 million. The apartment was advertised with two terraces and distant ocean views, but the promised delivery date passed without the home being completed. Although Undavia secured an arbitration decision directing the developer to refund his deposit with interest, he has reportedly still not received the money.He is not alone. According to The Coastal Star and The Real Deal, 13 buyers have filed lawsuits against the condominium developer over missed completion deadlines. Deposits in several cases have ranged from approximately $1 million to $2 million. Other cases have produced different outcomes. One couple obtained a judgment of approximately $1.98 million, while another buyer dispute involving Undavia and his wife was settled for $2.1 million, according to the South Florida Business Journal. A separate lawsuit filed in October 2026 by another prospective buyer seeking the return of a $1.23 million deposit highlights how the dispute continues to affect purchasers.The condominium tower is now at the centre of a major legal battle between Penn-Florida and its construction lenders. In July 2026, a lender group affiliated with Apollo Global Management filed a foreclosure lawsuit seeking approximately $417.7 million from the developer’s condominium-owning affiliate. The claim includes a $270 million loan principal, advances made toward project expenses, interest and other charges.The lenders allege that the developer defaulted on its loan obligations, missed repayment and construction deadlines, and failed to maintain the required hotel management agreement. Penn-Florida has challenged the lenders’ account. In a separate lawsuit seeking more than $500 million in damages, the developer alleges that the lenders interfered with construction decisions and withheld funding, contributing to the project’s difficulties. Those allegations remain disputed and have not been established as facts by a court. The adjoining hotel has also entered bankruptcy proceedings, adding another layer of uncertainty to the development.One of the biggest concerns for purchasers is whether they can recover money already released to the developer for construction. Florida law permits developers to use certain portions of condominium buyers’ deposits for construction when the relevant contractual conditions are met. Consequently, the amount a buyer can recover may depend on how the deposit was handled, the terms of the purchase agreement and the outcome of the legal proceedings.The foreclosure could complicate matters further because secured lenders generally have priority over many other creditors. Buyers whose deposits have already been spent may face a more difficult path to recovering their money than those whose funds remain protected in escrow. The dispute could also undermine the development’s luxury appeal. Mandarin Oriental issued a termination notice to Penn-Florida in 2025 over alleged contractual breaches, including unpaid expenses and reporting obligations. The developer maintains that its agreement with the brand remains in effect, leaving the residences’ branding uncertain.Penn-Florida has indicated that construction could resume and that some homes might be completed within nine months once work restarts. However, no clear restart date has been established. For buyers who invested millions in the promise of a finished luxury home, the immediate question is no longer simply when they can move in. It is whether they will receive their properties or recover the money they paid while the development’s future remains tied up in court.
Article Summary: Buyers are seeking refunds as the developer faces a $417.7 million foreclosure lawsuit. The development was marketed as an upscale destination combining luxury residences, hotel services and resort-style amenities. Buyers were also paying for the appeal of living in a property associated with the internationally recognised Mandarin Oriental hospitality brand.

Article Title: From 2014 to 2021, Wisconsin tracked three permeable pavements through seven winters; concrete pavers froze less often and thawed faster below ground
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image showing interlocking concrete pavers with melting snow and water around the joints, illustrating winter performance research on permeable pavements. Credits - Gemini

How the test was set up

What the temperature data showed

AI-generated representative image showing different permeable pavement surfaces and research monitoring equipment at a winter test site. Credits - Gemini

What it means for road salt

Winter is tough on highways in ways most drivers never notice. Water enters tiny cracks, freezes and expands, pushing the surface apart. The process can repeat when temperatures drop again. Cities using permeable surfaces to reduce flooding and pollution face another question: how do these pavements behave underground when temperatures remain below freezing?Seven winters of temperature data from Madison, Wisconsin, helped researchers examine how permeable pavements respond to cold weather. The US Geological Survey studied three types of permeable pavement: interlocking concrete pavers, pervious concrete and porous asphalt. The pavers had fewer days below freezing, higher temperatures during snowmelt, slower freezing and faster thawing than the other two surfaces. The findings were published in the journal Water in 2021.This is important, since ground that remains unfrozen is able to keep absorbing meltwater, rather than letting it pool on the surface and refreeze. That might ultimately mean less road salt; however, the researchers are quick to remind us that salt has its own set of concerns.The details of the experiment explain how the team came to that conclusion and where its boundaries are.In summer 2014, researchers established three test plots at a research site in Madison, Wisconsin, next to an overflow parking area. The plots represented interlocking concrete pavers, pervious concrete and porous asphalt. Each plot covered about 500 square feet, or 46.5 square metres, and had an aggregate base about 21 inches, or 53 centimetres, deep beneath the pavement. An impermeable liner and concrete walls separated the plots from the surrounding ground and from one another. The adjacent conventional parking area was not one of the three pavement types in the temperature comparison.Temperature monitoring ran from 21 August 2014 to 6 July 2021, with sensors recording readings every minute. Each plot had 27 thermocouples arranged at three depths: immediately below the pavement and 15 and 30 centimetres below the aggregate base. No vehicles drove on the test plots, and no salt or sand was applied to them. Snow deeper than 5 centimetres was removed with a hand-operated snow thrower, while the adjacent parking area was ploughed and treated with sand and salt. The main comparison used 303 winter days when sensors in all three plots were working at the same time.The main comparison covered 303 winter days with simultaneous readings from all three pavement types. The daily average air temperature was below freezing on 182 of those days. During those days, temperatures in the top, middle and bottom layers beneath the pavers remained above freezing on 42%, 68% and 81% of days, respectively. The corresponding figures were 20%, 38% and 74% for pervious concrete, and 25%, 45% and 74% for porous asphalt. These percentages are rounded summaries of the study data.Another measure counted days when the daily minimum air temperature stayed above freezing throughout the day. This occurred on only 39 of the 303 days. The bottom layer beneath the pavers stayed above freezing throughout the day on 263 days, compared with 214 days beneath pervious concrete and 212 days beneath porous asphalt.During the 120 days when the daily maximum air temperature remained below freezing, the top, middle and bottom layers beneath the pavers were also below freezing all day on 65, 35 and 14 days, respectively. The corresponding figures were 101, 82 and 35 days for pervious concrete, and 61, 58 and 28 days for porous asphalt. The porous asphalt top layer therefore had a similar number of frozen days to the pavers, but its lower layers froze more often.Researchers also examined three extended cold periods: the winter from late December 2014 to early March 2015 and two shorter periods in the winter of 2019 and 2020. During these periods, all depths beneath the pavers froze completely only once, while pervious concrete and porous asphalt froze completely during all three periods. Across the three pavement types, the top layer took an average of about 13 hours to freeze after air temperatures fell below zero. The middle layer took about one day and 15 hours, while the bottom layer took about three days and 22 hours. Thawing generally occurred faster than freezing, although the time varied by pavement type and depth.The researchers suggested that differences in construction may help explain the results. The gaps between the pavers occupy about 10% of the surface, while pores in pervious concrete and porous asphalt extend across their surfaces. The researchers proposed that the arrangement of the pavers, the movement of air and water through the gaps and aggregate base, and the thermal mass of the concrete blocks may affect heat transfer. These are possible explanations offered by the authors, rather than mechanisms independently established by the experiment. The darker, porous asphalt surface may also absorb more sunlight, helping explain why it stayed warmer near the surface than the previous concrete.These temperature differences matter during snowmelt. When the layers below a pavement remain above freezing, meltwater is more likely to infiltrate instead of pooling on the surface and refreezing. Researchers identified 137 melt days from meteorological records. Temperature data were available for 103 of those days for the pavers, 47 for pervious concrete and 89 for porous asphalt. On days with available data, the daily maximum temperature across all measured depths stayed above freezing on 96% of paver observations, 93% of porous asphalt observations and 83% of pervious concrete observations.The authors cited earlier studies reporting that permeable pavements could reduce road salt use. One study in Toronto reported about half as much salt use at a site with interlocking concrete pavers, while research in New Hampshire found that porous asphalt could maintain comparable or better surface conditions with 64% to 77% less salt than conventional asphalt.These findings do not mean that salt can be used without environmental consequences. Dissolved chloride can pass through permeable pavement and reach groundwater, even when the surface reduces runoff or the need for deicing. The researchers therefore recommended minimising salt use where possible and avoiding it when conditions permit.There are some boundaries to remember. The study was at a single site in one city, the plots were small, and nobody drove on them, so the findings reflect temperature behaviour rather than how well each surface handles traffic. The work was funded by various donors, including a foundation for teaching and research on interlocking concrete pavements, as well as Wisconsin agencies, the City of Madison and the USGS. The authors say the funders played no role in the findings. The findings suggest that all three permeable surfaces can retain temperature conditions that allow water to infiltrate during winter melt events, with interlocking pavers performing best in the temperature comparisons.
Article Summary: Seven winters of temperature data from Madison, Wisconsin, helped researchers examine how permeable pavements respond to cold weather. US Geological Survey studied three types of permeable pavement: interlocking concrete pavers, pervious concrete and porous asphalt. The pavers had fewer days below freezing, higher temperatures during snowmelt, slower freezing and faster thawing than the other two surfaces.

Article Title: In 2008, Minnesota tested pervious concrete on a road with light traffic; long-term monitoring found ride quality held up, while vacuuming helped maintain drainage
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image showing rainwater soaking into the textured surface of a pervious concrete road. Credits - Gemini

Why Minnesota did the trial

What years of testing showed

AI-generated representative image showing a specialised vacuum maintenance truck cleaning a porous concrete roadway to remove debris from its surface. Credits - Gemini

Why vacuuming matters

When rain falls on a typical road or parking lot, it has relatively few options for where to go. Because standard concrete and asphalt protect the ground, water flows into storm drains that frequently empty into rivers untreated after sliding off the surface and picking up oil and grit along the way. To address that, pervious concrete was created. Rainfall flows directly through the surface and soaks into the soil below because it is filled with many tiny, linked spaces.The idea made sense in theory, but engineers in cold climates had concerns. A surface full of holes may break up if water freezes within, and salt, snow ploughs and passing traffic could permanently block up the pores. So, to find out, Minnesota erected test portions on a low-usage route in 2008. Monitoring at MnROAD found that ride quality remained adequate for roads with light traffic over the years. MnDOT's research summary reports that regular vacuum maintenance, more than twice a year, helped maintain the pavement's benefits, including drainage.The results are most relevant to village lanes, driveways and residential streets that carry light traffic in snowy climates. The MnROAD tests found that ride quality remained suitable for roads with light traffic, while regular maintenance helped protect drainage.Researchers also recorded differences in smoothness and permeability between the test cells, so the findings should not be treated as a guarantee that every pervious concrete surface will perform the same way.To appreciate why the trial mattered, it helps to understand what officials were seeking to learn. Pervious pavements had promise for crowded metropolitan areas where enormous quantities of contaminated runoff end up in drains, but no one knew how they would handle Minnesota’s harsh environment, how much maintenance they would require or what their effect would be on groundwater quality. We got an early glimpse with a pervious concrete driveway completed in 2005.In autumn 2008, the team extended the work by installing three test sections on MnROAD's Low Volume Road, a two lane research loop about 2.5 miles (about 4 km) long. The design and early performance of the sections are documented in MnDOT's 2011 final report.Two of the cells were full-depth pervious concrete, one constructed on sandy soil and one on clay. The third was a porous concrete overlay about 4 inches (10 centimetres) thick on an existing slab. The full-depth cells are 7 inches (approximately 18 cm) of pervious concrete atop 4 inches of railway ballast and 8 inches of crushed stone.The loop functions like a laboratory. A five-axle semi-trailer weighing 80,000 pounds (about 36 tonnes) repeatedly travels along the inner lane, while the outer lane remains exposed to the weather. Crews plough and salt the route much like they would any low-volume road. Thermocouples and moisture sensors embedded in the cells track the frequency of ground freeze and thaw, the movement of temperatures through the layers and the effectiveness of water drainage.Researchers repeatedly measured ride quality, noise, friction, surface roughness, surface condition and permeability across seasons. During the first full year, friction readings taken with a smooth tyre ranged from 45 to 55, above the threshold of 25 that the report identified for corrective action.Noise readings on the pervious concrete cells ranged from 97 to 100.5 decibels, compared with about 103.5 decibels on a neighbouring concrete cell with transverse tining. The test results suggested that the porous surface absorbed more noise from the interaction between tyres and the road. Ride quality varied during the testing period. Reported roughness values ranged from 3.10 to 6.40 metres per kilometre, depending on the season, wheel path and measurement method. The report also noted that hand finishing during installation affected surface smoothness. Even so, MnDOT's longer-term analysis found that the test cells retained ride quality suitable for roads with light traffic.The cells did not behave identically. Researchers poured buckets of water onto the pavement and found that the wetting reached the full width of the inner lane but only about half the width of the outer lane. Separate density measurements suggested that the voids were unevenly distributed, with calculated porosity averaging from 13 to 19% in the cells. The report identified differences in construction and material inside the pores as possible explanations.Grit, leaves and winter sand can clog the connected pores, making maintenance important for drainage. In a demonstration about a year after construction, researchers used a vacuum truck with its brush switched off because mechanical brushing could push debris deeper into the gaps. The cells appeared relatively clean before the demonstration, and the drainage results changed only slightly after cleaning. The sandy subgrade cell continued to drain in 6 seconds, while the clay subgrade cell improved from 17 to 15.5 seconds.These results describe one demonstration and do not establish that regular maintenance is unnecessary or determine the ideal cleaning schedule. MnDOT's broader evaluation found that regular vacuuming more than twice a year helped maintain pervious pavement performance. Vacuuming and mechanical brushing are different procedures, so leaving the brush switched off during this test does not contradict the recommendation for recurring vacuum maintenance.The Minnesota trial does not establish that pervious concrete will work equally well on every road. It indicates that the material can be suitable for roads carrying light traffic in cold climates when installation is carefully controlled and drainage is maintained. The results also show why construction quality matters: differences in the distribution of pores and in surface smoothness affected the test cells. Anyone considering the material should account for local weather, traffic levels and the cost of regular vacuum maintenance.
Article Summary: Pervious pavements had promise for crowded metropolitan areas where enormous quantities of contaminated runoff end up in drains. But no one knew how they would handle Minnesota’s harsh environment, how much maintenance they would require or what their effect would be on groundwater quality. Minnesota erected test portions on a low- usage route in 2008.

Article Title: In 1989, Exxon Valdez spilled 11 million gallons off Alaska; 15 of 22 AT1 killer whales disappeared, and 37 years later, just seven remain
Article Text:
Prince William Sound, Southern Alaska. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The 22 AT1 whales counted in 1984 and the spill in spring 1989

Nine whales missing after 1989 and 15 presumed dead by 2003

Photo-identification from 1984 to 2010 and a survival dip in 1989 and 1990

Contrasting abundance and residency patterns of two sympatric populations of

transient killer whales

in the northern Gulf of Alaska

A killer whale surfaces in Prince William Sound, Alaska. The AT1 transient population declined from 22 whales in 1989 to seven in recent years. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Depleted status since June 2004 and seven whales photographed in 2019

Prince William Sound, on Alaska's southern coast, is a maze of fjords, islands and glacier-fed bays where harbor seals rest on shoreline rocks and floating ice. However, the mammal-eating orcas are called transients and biologists track individuals by the shapes and patterns on their dorsal fins and the white saddle patches behind them. Photographs taken during summer seasons produced catalogues detailed enough for scientists to determine which whales were alive in a given year.The small group of such transients, called AT1 by scientists, stays almost all the time in the Sound or in the adjacent Kenai Fjords. Because the group rarely leaves the region, most whales can be found each year, making the records more precise than estimates. Such a record became one of the most studied examples of consequences of the single technological disaster on the slow-reproducing marine mammal population.The federal report Alaska Marine Mammal Stock Assessments 2020 , prepared by NOAA scientists as technical memorandum NOAA-TM-AFSC-421, records that all 22 AT1 whales were counted for the first time in 1984 and were then seen every year through 1988, within a known range of about 200 miles that includes only Prince William Sound, the Kenai Fjords and adjacent offshore waters. In 1989, the Exxon Valdez ran aground on an underwater reef in the Sound and released about 11 million gallons of crude oil and Science News Explores notes that two killer whale groups were in the area at the time, AT1 being the first of them.AT1 is a distinct transient orca population, genetically different from resident killer whales and identified by a separate dialect. The spill’s effects piled onto an already stressed group: nine whales died in 1989, no calves have been documented since 1984 and the surviving males have been thinning out as they age.In addition, it is stated that nine AT1 whales were last seen in 1989 and have not been seen since 1990, while two additional whales have been missing since 1992, having last been seen in 1990 and 1991. Three of the missing whales, identified as AT5, AT7 and AT8, were among four members of the AT1 group photographed swimming near the Exxon Valdez tanker less than 24 hours after the oil spill, as documented in the research paper published in Human and Ecological Risk Assessment. Two carcasses found in 1989 and 1990 were genetically determined to belong to the AT1 population. This was followed by four older males, with one whale being found stranded in 2000, two whales being missing in 2002 and one whale being missing in 2003. All AT1 whales missing for at least four years have never been resighted, which is why NOAA considers all 15 missing whales to be dead. It is added that the majority of deaths occurred in 1989 and 1990.The second study,, appeared in Fishery Bulletin in 2012. These researchers identified whales through photographs taken over a period of 27 years from 1984 to 2010 and made 203 sightings of AT1 whales.According to their mark-recapture analyses, survival between 1989 and 1990 decreased to a median of 0.68, which is in contrast to the overall survival rate of 0.99 for the whole research period and abundance fell dramatically from the 22 whales present before the spill in 1989 to just seven whales at the end of the study period in 2010, the same seven that remained after the last disappearance in 2003. 97% of posterior probability was assigned to the period of abundance change within five years following 1989. The researchers concluded that the decline reflected deaths rather than departures, since AT1 whales rarely left the study site, which is consistent with NOAA’s presumption that the missing whales are dead.As noted above, the AT1 stock was declared depleted under the Marine Mammal Protection Act on June 3, 2004. The Exxon Valdez Oil Spill Trustee Council’s long-term killer whale monitoring project confirmed through surveys and contributed photographs that all seven remaining AT1 whales had survived to 2019. The decrease from 22 whales recorded in 1989 to seven works out to a 68.2% decline. No new births have been documented since 1984 and it is determined that the recovery of the stock is unlikely. It should be emphasized that the spill is not considered to be the sole reason for the depletion. As noted above, the 2012 study identifies AT1 as a remnant stock whose path toward extinction has been accelerated by the losses caused by the spill. In addition, its authors indicate that harbor seals, which were the main food source, decreased significantly in number in the study area during this time frame, although no numbers are provided.
Article Summary: AT1 is a distinct transient orca population, genetically different from resident killer whales and identified by a separate dialect. In 1989, the Exxon Valdez ran aground on an underwater reef in the Sound and released about 11 million gallons of crude oil. The spill’s effects piled onto an already stressed group: nine whales died in 1989, no calves have been documented since 1984 and the surviving males have been thinning out as they age.

Article Title: In 2017, Alaska laid steel-fiber rubber concrete panels on Abbott Road; field tests found less rutting than nearby asphalt, while laboratory tests indicated freeze-thaw resistance
Article Text:
AI Representation: A clean, smooth concrete pavement section contrasts with heavily rutted asphalt along a road framed by scenic Alaskan mountains and spruce trees. Image credits: Chatgpt

Laboratory and cast-in-place results that preceded the road test

Use of Steel Fiber-Reinforced Rubberized Concrete in Cold Regions

Precast panel installation on Abbott Road in summer 2017

Phase II field comparison with hot mix asphalt on the adjacent section

Planned monitoring from 2017 to 2020 and use at intersections

Precast concrete panels are manufactured off site and installed as finished roadway sections. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Anyone who has driven through a cold northern city at the end of winter knows how quickly a road surface can lose its shape. Wear comes from studded tires, meltwater that seeps into cracks and refreezes overnight and heavy vehicles repeatedly traveling the same wheel paths at intersections. Rutting, the formation of grooves known as ruts in the wheel paths, is a typical problem of asphalt under repeated loads.This issue has always been present in Anchorage and local engineers have been studying for a long time what surface material could withstand the stress at the intersection point and other high-traffic areas. While concrete does not change its shape, it is known for cracking due to changing temperatures. Rubber, used together with concrete, makes it more elastic, but decreases some of its mechanical properties. To compensate for it, the Alaskan researchers introduced short steel fibers. Such material was studied in the laboratory and on the real road and the results of both experiments are presented in this paper.The first study,, appears in the U.S. Department of Transportation’s ROSAP repository with a December 24, 2017 date and it describes the research as beginning with laboratory wheel tracker and freeze-thaw testing, followed by a small experimental cast-in-place panel trial.The abstract reports that wheel tracker tests showed much lower rutting for SFRRC than for asphalt and that freeze-thaw testing showed less cracking and strength reduction than for Portland cement concrete. The team ran these laboratory tests at the University of Alaska Anchorage, where an experimental cast-in-place panel then showed little wear under traffic, a result that informed the design of the pre-cast panels for Abbott Road.The precast panels for the Abbott Road project were designed, built and installed in summer 2017. The ROSAP study says the Abbott Road installation was meant to test at full scale, on a high-traffic urban arterial road, what the laboratory and campus results had suggested about rutting, freeze-thaw durability, construction process and life cycle cost.
