The study also says the panels would be monitored to determine whether SFRRC could be used on roadways.The research section of the Alaska Department of Transportation & Public Facilities website hosts this second report, which contains the practical field evaluation of the SFRRC. The Phase II report compared the SFRRC sections with adjoining hot mix asphalt sections. The main findings of the summary were that SFRRC road surfaces had considerable rutting resistance when compared to the adjoining asphalt samples. The freeze-thaw results were stated in the same part, which was also tested against the lab results from the earlier cited test.The December 2017 study covers the laboratory and cast-in-place work and the Abbott Road plan; the Phase II report documents the field comparison findings; and the broader program, scheduled to run through December 31, 2020, was set out separately. A project listing at the National Concrete Pavement Technology Center describes an experimental feature evaluation of the SFRRC installed on Abbott Road, sponsored by the Federal Highway Administration and led by researcher Carolyn Morehouse. This listing has a start date of January 1, 2017 and an end date of December 31, 2020. In addition, it states that data will be collected for three years following construction for material wear, operation and pavement conditions, with comparisons from control sites.After this period, a synopsis was to be prepared that would include recommendations on the use of SFRRC in Alaska and it might also address issues that better specification and construction and maintenance practices could have prevented. Phase II evaluated SFRRC on a public road and the research recommended its further use at highway intersections and in test sections on major arterial roads, as described in the 2023 study published in the Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering.
Article Summary: Steel Fiber-Reinforced Rubberized Concrete (SFRRC) is a new type of concrete used in Alaska. SFRRC is more elastic, but decreases some of its mechanical properties. Researchers tested the material in the laboratory and on the real road. Wheel tracker tests showed much lower rutting for SFR RC than for asphalt.

Article Title: 6 children among 12 injured in shooting near Florida university stadium
Article Text:
At least 12 individuals were injured in a shooting incident that occurred in Tallahassee (Photo: AP).

At least 12 people, including six children, were injured in a shooting near a football stadium in Tallahassee, Florida, on Saturday night during homecoming weekend at Florida A&M University (FAMU), authorities said.11 victims sustained gunshot wounds, while at least three suffered serious injuries, according to police. One victim was in critical condition, while eight others were reported to be stable, Reuters reported.The shooting occurred shortly before 8 pm near Perry and Manatee streets, close to FAMU's Bragg Memorial Stadium, following a football game, the Tallahassee Democrat reported.Tallahassee police chief Lawrence Revell said a preliminary investigation indicated that an altercation had taken place between individuals before the shooting. No arrests had been made, he said.“I stand before you tonight devastated,” Revell told reporters at a late-night press conference.Addressing the victims and their families, he added, “We hurt with you, and we will continue to get you the answers you so desperately want.”“My message to the community is this... No family should have to experience this kind of violence, this kind of fear, this kind of heartbreak,” he said.Revell also praised first responders for their efforts to assist the injured amid the chaos. He said officers had carried victims in their arms to get them to help because the crowds made it difficult to move through the area.“We had officers who were picking up victims and carrying them in their arms to transport because they couldn't get through the mass of people,” he said.Revell stressed the importance of people dispersing from the scene to allow officers to reach victims. He said the first responders had rushed towards the danger without knowing where the shooters were or how many people had been injured.FAMU said in a social media post that the shooting occurred near its campus but that the university remained safe.
Article Summary: At least 12 people, including six children, were injured in a shooting near a football stadium in Tallahassee, Florida. 11 victims sustained gunshot wounds, while at least three suffered serious injuries, according to police. One victim was in critical condition, while eight others were reported to be stable.

Article Title: 'France is burning down': Trump blames immigration policies amid protests, mass arrests
Article Text:
During a recent rally, Donald Trump voiced his disapproval of France's immigration policies, coinciding with widespread protests that saw nearly 1,000 arrests due to rising living costs. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Nearly 1,000 arrests during protests across France

Macron hits back at foreign leaders' remarks

Netanyahu accuses France of failing to tackle extremism

US president Donald Trump criticised France’s immigration policies during a campaign rally for republican candidates in Perry, Georgia, on Saturday, claiming the country was facing turmoil because it had opened its borders to people hostile towards it, according to the news agency ANI.“France is right now burning down because it opens its borders to people who hate it,” Trump said, alleging that immigrants disliked the country’s buildings, monuments, paintings and culture.Drawing a comparison with US immigration policy, Trump told the gathering that such individuals should never be allowed into a country. “And that's what we're doing,” he added.His remarks came as early voting began for the November 2026 US midterm elections, which will determine control of both chambers of Congress and influence the remainder of Trump's legislative agenda.Meanwhile, nearly 1,000 people were arrested during demonstrations across France on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, warning that the figure could rise further.The protests, fuelled by anger over the rising cost of living and concerns about education funding, witnessed clashes between demonstrators and police in Paris and several other cities.According to France 24, the French government estimated that around 410,000 people participated in demonstrations nationwide, while organisers put the turnout at nearly 800,000.Authorities said the demonstration in Paris had been completely dispersed along the Cours de Vincennes after confrontations between protesters and law enforcement officers towards the rear of the march.The prefectural police said a Gendarmerie helicopter had been deployed to assist ground personnel and locate any remaining groups of rioters. Officials estimated that more than 500 people involved in rioting were present towards the end of the demonstration.Police used water cannons and tear gas grenades after projectiles were thrown at officers.“As I speak to you, we are at nearly 1,000 arrests,” Nunez said during a press briefing, adding that the number was likely to increase significantly. He noted that 385 arrests had been recorded by the same time the previous Saturday, when protests were also marked by violence and looting.Although several gatherings began peacefully, clashes intensified in Paris later on Saturday. Confrontations were also reported in major cities, including Lyon, Lille, Marseille, Montpellier, Nantes and Toulouse, Euronews reported.The demonstrations brought together a broad coalition of left-wing political leaders, trade unions, student organisations, activists and non-governmental organisations, including Amnesty International, according to France 24.French president Emmanuel Macron had criticised foreign leaders for using unrest in France to advance their own political agendas. Speaking in Doha on October 21 during a three-day visit to Qatar and the wider Gulf region, Macron appeared to take aim at Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu without initially naming them.“There are people who campaign at France's expense — leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic,” Macron said, according to Euronews.The French president's visit focused on securing energy supplies amid the country's cost-of-living pressures.Trump had previously described France as being “under siege, looted and set ablaze by migrants, jihadists and communists”, warning US voters that similar consequences could follow if Democrats won the midterm elections.Macron rejected claims that foreign interference had triggered the violence, while criticising what he described as misleading narratives and AI-driven misinformation surrounding the unrest.“As far as I'm concerned, there is no visible foreign interference in the events that took place. There has been foreign manipulation of information in the aftermath, which led to equally unacceptable and stupid comments from many people, including foreign leaders,” he said.When a reporter asked whether his comments were directed at Trump, Macron replied, “Among others, yes.”He also urged foreign leaders not to aggravate tensions and defended France against criticism from abroad.“In these moments, we see who loves France and who doesn't. And the fact is, all the people who are speaking ill of our country right now are people who do not love our country. So, those people really bother me,” he added.Netanyahu had also criticised the French government's handling of the unrest. In an interview with French-language broadcaster i24News on October 20, the Israeli prime minister claimed France was facing an “invasion of extremist Islam”, according to the Times of Israel.Accusing French authorities of failing to prepare adequately for the disorder, Netanyahu said, “They did not prepare in time; they simply gave up. They succumbed to the invasion of extremist Islam.”Asked what France should do, he urged the country to resist extremist groups rather than pursue a policy of appeasement.The protests in France began more than a month ago, with students raising concerns about conditions in high schools, teacher shortages, school schedules and inequalities between public and private education, France 24 reported.The movement subsequently expanded into a broader national mobilisation involving trade unions, civil society groups and the Yellow Vests movement. It gathered further momentum following violent clashes during cost-of-living demonstrations the previous week.
Article Summary: Nearly 1,000 people were arrested during protests across France on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. Clashes between demonstrators and police were reported in Paris and several other cities. French president Emmanuel Macron had criticised foreign leaders for using unrest in France to advance their own political agendas.

Article Title: In 1906, a gold discovery attracted 700 people to Skidoo, California, turning it into a $1.5 million mining hub before the boom ended and residents left just after a decade
Article Text:
Skidoo Mill. Image Credit: Western Mining history/Website

Skidoo attracted 700 people after the 1906 gold discovery

A long pipeline helped the mining operation grow

How much gold revenue did Skidoo produce

Skidoo's prosperity faded after 1917

The surviving mill preserves Skidoo's mining history

A gold discovery in 1906 transformed a remote part of California's Death Valley region into a busy mining settlement. Skidoo attracted hundreds of people hoping to make their fortunes, eventually growing to a population of around 700. The town became one of the area's most important gold-mining centres, producing approximately $1.5 million in revenue during its main period of activity. However, the settlement's success depended on difficult mining conditions and the ability to transport water across the desert. As mining activity declined, residents gradually left, turning Skidoo into a ghost town.According to the US National Park Service, two prospectors discovered gold in the area in 1906. Their find attracted interest in a region where mining offered the possibility of substantial financial rewards, despite the challenges of working in a remote desert environment.Skidoo developed in the Panamint Mountains within what is now Death Valley National Park. Its growth formed part of a wider period of renewed interest in gold and silver mining across the Death Valley region during the early 20th century.Skidoo was the region's largest mining operation between 1907 and 1917. The settlement reached a population of approximately 700, with people arriving to work in the mines and support the growing community.Western Mining History also reports that Skidoo had a newspaper, a bank, a school and telephone service at its height in 1907. These facilities reflected how quickly a remote mining camp developed into a functioning town.The settlement's growth was not simply a result of the gold discovery. Extracting the metal required infrastructure, workers and a reliable supply of water, all of which had to be established in a challenging landscape.One of Skidoo's biggest challenges was obtaining enough water to process the gold-bearing rock. The town's location in an arid region made a dependable supply essential to its mining activities.The National Park Service states that a 23-mile metal pipeline was constructed to carry water to the mill and the town. The system connected the mining operation with a distant water source, allowing the processing facility to operate in an otherwise dry environment.Western Mining History describes the pipeline as an important undertaking associated with mine owner Bob Montgomery. Water was carried from Birch Spring, high on the western side of Telescope Peak, to the mill. The pipeline provided water to prospectors exploring isolated parts of the desert.Building such a system required considerable investment and planning. Without a steady water supply, the operation would have struggled to process ore on a large scale. The pipeline therefore became a crucial part of Skidoo's development, supporting both gold extraction and activity in the surrounding area.The mill opened in 1907, according to the National Park Service. Its purpose was to extract gold from the ore brought from the mines. The construction of the facility marked an important step in turning the original discovery into a more organised mining enterprise.Skidoo became one of California's notable gold-mining settlements during its relatively short period of prosperity. The NPS estimates that the operation generated about $1.5 million in revenue during its main mining years.The figure illustrates the scale of the operation, although it represents historical revenue rather than the town's value in modern money. It also shows that Skidoo's success rested on more than a single discovery, with numerous mining claims contributing to the area's output.Production continued as miners worked to extract gold from the surrounding deposits. In September 1908, the Los Angeles Herald reported that gold bricks worth $10,000 from the Skidoo mines had arrived in nearby Rhyolite before being sent to the mint. The shipment represented 15 days of production and was considered typical of the preceding 3 months.The ore was also increasing in both quantity and quality at the time. However, the revenue figures alone do not capture the practical difficulties of operating in the desert.The mining boom eventually lost momentum. According to the NPS, Skidoo was the Death Valley region's largest mining operation from 1907 to 1917, but most residents moved away after 1917.The decline reflected the uncertain nature of mining settlements, whose fortunes depended heavily on the continued viability of local mineral deposits. Once the main period of activity ended, the town could no longer sustain the population and services that had developed around the mines.Mining did not stop completely when residents began leaving. Sporadic milling continued until 1942, when Skidoo was completely abandoned. Western Mining History notes that mining took place in the district again during the 1930s, demonstrating that interest in its gold deposits persisted even after the original town had largely disappeared.Nevertheless, these later efforts did not restore Skidoo to its earlier prominence.Today, Skidoo forms part of the historic mining landscape within Death Valley National Park. Although the town itself has largely disappeared, remnants of its industrial past remain visible.NPS identifies the Skidoo Historic District as a site listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Its surviving features include tanks, mercury tables and substantial portions of the mill operations. The structure provides evidence of the equipment and infrastructure required to extract gold in the early 20th century.The site also illustrates the lasting environmental challenges associated with historical mining. The NPS is investigating the Skidoo Mill site for potential cleanup of hazardous chemicals.
Article Summary: Skidoo developed in the Panamint Mountains within what is now Death Valley National Park. Two prospectors discovered gold in the area in 1906. Skidoo attracted hundreds of people hoping to make their fortunes. The town became one of the area's most important gold-mining centres. It produced approximately $1.5 million in revenue during its main period of activity.

Article Title: Two cottonmouth snakes were filmed entwined in Alabama water; online commenters said the venomous pair were male rivals fighting, not mating
Article Text:
Image:r/snakes/Reddit

Original poster watched the Alabama cottonmouths for ten minutes and found them together an hour later

Cottonmouth snake (Image: Wikipedia)

Commenters dispute the mating claim and describe a territorial duel between two male cottonmouths

Reddit users amazed by male combat in water as one predicts a female is waiting to breed with the winner

Image: Wikipedia

Similar snake fights mistaken for mating were reported at Colorado's Garden of the Gods and in Greece

What the Alabama cottonmouth video shows about reading snake behaviour from an online video

Cottonmouth snakes intertwined in the water near Birmingham, Alabama, have sparked an online debate over whether the venomous pair were mating or fighting over territory. Footage of the pair shared on Reddit's Snakes community shows them entwined yet almost calm, which led the person who posted it to suspect courtship. Fellow snake enthusiasts quickly disagreed in the comments, describing the encounter as a contest between rival males. The clip was recorded just south of the city, and the disagreement over its meaning has turned a strange sighting into a small lesson in telling territorial combat apart from courtship between snakes.According to The Cool Down, the original poster told Reddit's Snakes community they felt compelled to share the sighting and were fairly certain it was mating, while admitting they might be wrong. That hedge matters, because it left the thread open to correction. The poster later told commenters they had watched the pair for a good ten minutes and that the snakes were not being particularly aggressive with one another.The poster was working nearby at the time. After leaving to carry on with that work and returning about an hour later, they said the two were still together, doing what they could only describe as cuddling.Soon after the footage appeared, commenters streamed into the thread to challenge the idea that the snakes were mating. The reaction was swift enough that the debate was well under way before the poster added their later observations. One commenter told the original poster the pair were two males in combat, while another told the thread it looked like a "territorial thumb war on water." The second remark is a joke, but it neatly captures the reading that took hold in the thread, a standoff between two rivals rather than a courtship.Other commenters told the thread they were amazed that the territorial display took place in such an unusual location. One said they had never seen male combat in water and urged others to watch their step, because a female would probably be nearby, waiting to breed with the winner of the duel. Another commenter joked that it was possibly the first footage they had seen of naval combat between vipers. The mixture of astonishment and wordplay shows how the footage was received: as an unusual sight worth enjoying as much as analysing.People have made the same mix-up elsewhere, The Cool Down noted in May this year, at Colorado's Garden of the Gods, snakes taken to be mating were in fact battling for breeding rights. At Sitia Geopark in Greece, two males fighting over turf looked like an exotic mating ritual. The same article also pointed readers to a different kind of sighting in India, where a king cobra was filmed making an elegant glide along the shoreline.The episode shows how quickly an inaccurate description can be corrected when footage is shared publicly. The poster offered a guess and admitted uncertainty, other users supplied a competing explanation within the same thread, and the poster then added fuller observations of their own. Even though the original account was inaccurate, the pair's calm demeanour explains why the mistake was easy to make.
Article Summary: Footage of the pair shared on Reddit's Snakes community shows them entwined yet almost calm, which led the person who posted it to suspect courtship. Fellow snake enthusiasts quickly disagreed in the comments, describing the encounter as a contest between rival males.

Article Title: For 20 years, a former New Jersey military housing site sat abandoned; now a $70 million plan will replace the decaying complex with 275 homes and new shops near Netflix's planned $1 billion studio
Article Text:
The development offers easy access to Asbury Park, Long Branch, and commuter rail connections to New York City.

From military housing to a new community

Netflix's billion-dollar bet

Homes, shops and shore access

A cautious moment for construction

For two decades, a stretch of Eatontown, New Jersey, stood as a reminder of a community left behind. Once home to military families, the abandoned Howard Commons site gradually deteriorated, its vacant buildings and neglected grounds becoming an eyesore along Pinebrook Road. Now, the long-neglected property is set for a dramatic transformation, with developers betting that new homes, shops and a nearby Netflix production campus could help usher in a new chapter for the region.According to reports by the New York Post and Realtordot com, developers have broken ground on The Premiere at Monmouth, a $70 million residential and retail development planned for the former military housing site. The project will bring 275 homes alongside a public park, grocery store, convenience store and gas station, creating a new neighbourhood as Eatontown prepares for a wave of investment and employment opportunities.According to New York Post, Howard Commons was once part of the former Fort Monmouth military installation, providing housing for hundreds of military families. Following years of vacancy and deterioration, the property became a symbol of stalled redevelopment.The latest plan, developed through an agreement between the borough and Lennar Corp., aims to replace the decaying complex with a community designed around contemporary residential needs, the report adds.The new development is expected to include single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums, catering to a range of prospective buyers, from first-time homeowners to families seeking additional space. The inclusion of everyday retail and public green space is intended to make the project more than a housing complex, giving residents access to essential services and shared outdoor areas, the New York report explains.As reported by Realtor dot com, Lennar has worked with the Fort Monmouth Economic Revitalization Authority since the early 2000s and identified the long-vacant site as an opportunity for redevelopment. The developer is now positioning the project as part of a broader revival of Monmouth County.A major factor behind the renewed interest in the area is Netflix's planned studio complex at Fort Monmouth. The streaming giant broke ground on its $1 billion Netflix Studios East project in 2025, transforming part of the former US Army installation into a major East Coast production hub, Realtor report explains.Scheduled to open in 2028, the 292-acre campus is expected to feature 12 sound stages covering nearly 500,000 square feet, alongside facilities supporting other production activities and community amenities. The project is anticipated to generate jobs and attract businesses serving the entertainment industry, strengthening the region's prospects as a growing centre for film and television production, adds the report by New York Post and Realtor too.The Premiere at Monmouth is about a 10-minute drive from the planned studio campus. Developers are hoping that proximity to the facility will appeal to buyers looking to live near future employment opportunities and the businesses expected to follow.The area's housing market has already shown signs of heightened demand. In May, NJ dot com reported that a five-bedroom home in nearby Little Silver sold for $2.6 million, approximately 24% above its $2.1 million asking price. The sale offers a glimpse of the competition emerging in communities within easy reach of Fort Monmouth.Beyond the studio connection, The Premiere at Monmouth benefits from its location near established Jersey Shore destinations, including Asbury Park and Long Branch. The Red Bank train station also provides NJ Transit connections for commuters travelling towards New York City, adding to the development's appeal for people balancing suburban living with work in the metropolitan area.According to Realtor dot com, early interest has come from a broad mix of buyers, with appointments for prospective purchasers expected to begin in late autumn. The project also offers an opportunity to give a neglected former military site a renewed civic purpose.The redevelopment arrives amid uncertainty in the wider US housing market. September figures cited in the reports showed building permits slipping 0.2% from August and 3% year over year. Housing starts fell 5.2% month over month and 7.4% annually, while completions declined 2.2% from the previous month and 14% compared with the same period a year earlier.Against the backdrop of elevated mortgage rates and construction costs, The Premiere at Monmouth represents a significant local investment. Its success will depend on whether housing demand, infrastructure and the anticipated economic benefits of Netflix's studio come together as expected. For Eatontown, however, the groundbreaking marks a visible shift: a site that spent 20 years in decline is finally being prepared for a new generation of residents, concludes the report.Images Courtesy: Realtor and Google Maps
Article Summary: Developers have broken ground on The Premiere at Monmouth, a $70 million residential and retail development planned for the former military housing site. Howard Commons was once part of the former Fort Monmouth military installation, providing housing for hundreds of military families. The new development is expected to include single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums, catering to a range of prospective buyers.

Article Title: ‘Maybe tomorrow’: Trump hints at fresh Iran strikes as Tehran denies Hormuz deal offer
Article Text:
Donald Trump has hinted at a possible US attack on Iran as soon as Sunday while keeping open the possibility of a deal.

Iran denies offering to reopen Strait of Hormuz

US President Donald Trump has hinted at the possibility of renewed military action against Iran as early as Sunday, while keeping the door open to a diplomatic agreement. Tehran, however, has denied reports that it offered to reopen the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz in exchange for Washington lifting its naval blockade.Speaking to reporters after casting his ballot in Florida on Saturday, Trump said Iran wanted a deal to reopen the waterway but questioned whether Tehran would honour any agreement.“Do you really think I would tell you that? Maybe tomorrow... There's a possibility I will. There's also a possibility we'll have a nice, big, beautiful agreement,” Trump said when asked about the prospect of fresh strikes.“They want to make a deal, but the problem is, will they hold the deal?” he added.Trump also reiterated his hardline position towards Tehran at a campaign rally in Florida, warning that the US could launch another military operation if Iran failed to reach an agreement.“We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree,” he told the cheering crowd, referring to the previous US military campaign against Iran.“If they're smart, they'll just say, 'Let's get down to business.' But, you know, I doubt they'll do that because perhaps they're not smart,” he added.Iran has rejected reports that it proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its naval blockade.The IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency said Tehran had made no fresh proposal to Pakistani mediators, describing reports by a Saudi Arabian outlet claiming that Iran had conveyed such an offer to Washington through Pakistan as a “lie and fabrication”, Press TV reported.The denial follows reports that Iran was willing to reopen the strategic waterway if Washington ended its blockade.On October 18, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remained on the table. Speaking to Iranian media in Baghdad, he said the US had shared comments on the proposal that Tehran was reviewing.“Our situation is clear and based on the seven-days proposal presented to the US. They shared comments which we are reviewing… If there is any honesty on the US part, which there isn’t, the way to reopening the Strait of Hormuz is obvious,” Araghchi said.The latest denial comes as Washington continues to signal that a diplomatic settlement is possible, even as Trump keeps the threat of further strikes alive.
Article Summary: Iran denies offering to reopen Strait of Hormuz in exchange for US lifting naval blockade. US President Donald Trump hints at renewed military action against Iran as early as Sunday. But he also leaves the door open to a diplomatic agreement. Tehran has denied reports that it offered to reopen the strategically vital waterway.

Article Title: Pakistan reopens Iran border after week-long halt to commercial traffic
Article Text:
Following a week-long closure due to security threats, Pakistan has reopened the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing with Iran.

Security concerns preceded reopening

Pakistan has resumed cross-border trade with Iran through a major border point in Balochistan after a seven-day shutdown disrupted cargo movement, left transporters stranded and raised concerns about LPG availability as winter approaches.Commercial traffic restarted on Saturday at the Gabd-Rimdan crossing in Gwadar district, Dawn reported. Officials permitted the movement of import and export consignments carrying consignment notes issued on or before October 16. according to the news agency PTI.Mir Naveed Jan Kalmati, head of the Gwadar chamber of commerce and industry, confirmed that the crossing, also called Gate 250, was operational again.Kalmati said trucks and other vehicles carrying commercial goods were now permitted to travel in both directions between Pakistan and Iran.Welcoming the reopening, he said it would offer relief to traders and transport operators who had been unable to move their cargo during the closure. The restoration of supplies could also help address Pakistan's LPG shortage and ease pressure on rising food and energy costs.The crossing was shut on October 17 by Pakistan's commerce ministry, which did not publicly disclose the reason for the suspension. However, security concerns were believed to have prompted the move.The disruption affected LPG supplies at a time when demand for the fuel generally increases during the colder months.The situation worsened on Thursday when unidentified gunmen attacked trucks parked near the Gabd-Rimdan crossing. Dozens of vehicles were reportedly set ablaze, while several others sustained damage.Local authorities reviewed the security situation before allowing trade to resume on Saturday. Additional security personnel have been deployed to safeguard commercial convoys travelling through the area.The reopening also follows a visit to Iran earlier this week by Pakistan Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, who held discussions with Iranian leaders on bilateral ties and regional developments.Pakistan and Iran share a 909-km frontier between Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province and Pakistan's Balochistan province. The border crossings are vital channels for trade and the movement of goods between the neighbouring countries.
Article Summary: Commercial traffic restarted on Saturday at the Gabd-Rimdan crossing in Gwadar district, Dawn reported. Officials permitted the movement of import and export consignments carrying consignment notes issued on or before October 16. The disruption affected LPG supplies at a time when demand for the fuel generally increases.

Article Title: 'Islamabad arming Afghans to fight anti-Pakistani insurgents': Ex-US envoy sounds alarm
Article Text:
The allegations come amid worsening ties between Islamabad and Kabul

Former US envoy Zalmay Khalilzad has sounded the alarm over reports that Islamabad is recruiting Afghans to fight anti-Pakistan insurgents, warning that relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan are likely to deteriorate further.“There have been many reports that Pakistan is arming Afghans to fight the Taliban in Afghanistan. Now there are reports that the Pakistani military is recruiting Afghans to fight against anti-Pakistan insurgents. As things currently stand, relations between #Afghanistan and #Pakistan are likely to get much worse,” Khalilzad wrote.Pakistan's information ministry on Saturday rejected Khalilzad's allegations as “baseless and misleading”, accusing him of promoting a narrative in support of the Taliban government in Afghanistan.The allegations come amid worsening ties between Islamabad and Kabul, with repeated border clashes and Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan adding to tensions this year.On Saturday, Pakistani forces and Afghan Taliban personnel exchanged fire at several locations along the north-western border. Pakistani security officials and state-run media said troops, backed by artillery, destroyed Taliban posts during hours of fighting in Kurram district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.Pakistani officials also claimed that troops killed an unspecified number of Pakistani Taliban militants attempting to cross into Pakistan from eastern Afghanistan. Kabul did not immediately comment on the clashes.Pakistan has accused Afghanistan of providing sanctuary to leaders and fighters of the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which is separate from but closely allied with the Afghan Taliban. Kabul has denied the allegations. The continuing violence has further strained relations between the two countries.
Article Summary: Zalmay Khalilzad warns that relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan are likely to deteriorate further. The allegations come amid worsening ties between Islamabad and Kabul. On Saturday, Pakistani forces and Afghan Taliban personnel exchanged fire at several locations along the north-western border.

Article Title: 'Pak defeated, cannot fight us': Baloch rebels launch fresh strike; several killed
Article Text:
The group also claimed to have taken control of the Muzhani police station

The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has claimed responsibility for a series of strikes against Pakistani security forces, alleging that its fighters killed a Military Intelligence (MI) captain and several personnel of the Pakistan Army’s Special Services Group (SSG) during its ongoing Operation Almas.In a press release issued by its spokesperson, Major Gwahram Baloch, the separatist group claimed that Pakistani forces had suffered significant human and material losses at multiple locations and were forced to retreat following clashes. The BLF, as cited by news agency ANI said that the operation was continuing on several fronts with “full intensity and success”.Videos purportedly showing the ongoing violence have also surfaced. In one clip, a woman is heard saying, “Pakistan is defeated now & and cannot fight us”, as gunfire continues in the background. Another video showed a woman firing what appeared to be an assault rifle.The BLF further claimed that its fighters had overrun the main camp of the Frontier Works Organization (FWO) and hoisted the organisation’s flag at Gwadar Zero Point, describing the development as evidence of its advances during the operation.The group also claimed to have taken control of the Muzhani police station, seizing official weapons and military equipment. It alleged that a police official was killed during the confrontation.In a separate incident in Gubd, the BLF said its fighters attacked a convoy of Pakistani security forces, destroying an army vehicle and killing or injuring several personnel travelling in it. The group also claimed that its fighters had taken control of the police checkpoint at Gubd Cross.
Article Summary: The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has claimed responsibility for a series of strikes against Pakistani security forces. The group alleges that its fighters killed a Military Intelligence (MI) captain and several personnel of the Pakistan Army’s Special Services Group (SSG)

Article Title: Pakistan's elite want out? Khawaja Asif flags bureaucrats' alleged exit plans to foreign shores
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan defence minister Khwaja Asif

Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif has questioned the loyalty of senior bureaucrats, alleging that several government officials planned to settle abroad while serving the country, according to a report by Pakistan's Express Tribune.In a post on X, Asif said Pakistan had capable and honest bureaucrats, but alleged that many officials had made Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom and other European countries their permanent homes over the past several years.He claimed some officers had prepared for their relocation under a deliberate plan while employed by the Pakistani government. Portugal, he said, had emerged as a destination for what he described as a bureaucratic exodus in recent years. He added that he had raised the issue on social media a few months ago.Asif said the officers whose names had surfaced in connection with the matter had held important positions and remained close to successive governments. He also alleged that an individual who facilitated permanent residency arrangements had fled after collecting substantial sums of money from several influential bureaucrats.The minister did not identify the officials or provide details to substantiate the allegations. He said troubling accounts were circulating about the matter and questioned whether senior officials who had enjoyed the privileges and respect associated with public service had remained committed to Pakistan.“Does it rise above all doubt and suspicion, or are they merely in transit?” Asif asked, questioning whether such officials viewed Pakistan as their permanent home or merely a temporary stop before settling abroad.
Article Summary: Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif has questioned the loyalty of senior bureaucrats. He alleges that several government officials planned to settle abroad while serving the country. Portugal has emerged as a destination for what he described as a bureaucratic exodus in recent years. He also alleged that an individual who facilitated permanent residency arrangements had fled.

Article Title: Pakistan army officer killed in IED blast during Balochistan operation
Article Text:
Pakistan Army major killed in Balochistan IED blast as security forces eliminate four terrorists.

A Pakistan Army major was killed in an improvised explosive device (IED) blast during a security operation in Balochistan province, while security forces killed four terrorists in a separate operation, the military said on Monday.According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the military's media wing, security forces conducted operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Gwadar and Jattakabad in Kalat district on Sunday following reports of terrorist presence.During an operation in Jattakabad, the forces killed four terrorists and recovered “a large cache of arms and ammunition”, the Army said.In a separate action, security forces carried out clearance operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Pasni in Gwadar district. During the operation, 34-year-old Major Wajahat Waheed was killed in an IED attack while leading the operation.“Sanitisation operations will continue to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area,” the Army said.The military added that security forces and law enforcement agencies remained committed to eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism in the country.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to the security forces for killing the four terrorists and expressed grief over the death of the officer.“Major Wajahat Waheed sacrificed his life for the protection of our beloved homeland; the nation is proud of its brave son,” the prime minister said.Sharif also extended condolences to the officer's family and prayed for the elevation of his rank.Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, with security forces continuing operations to contain the violence.A day earlier, security forces killed eight terrorists during operations in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts.(With inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Pakistan Army major killed in Balochistan IED blast as security forces eliminate four terrorists. Major Wajahat Waheed was killed in an IED attack while leading the operation. Security forces carried out clearance operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Pasni in Gwadar district.

Article Title: US-designated LeT terrorist dies after mysteriously falling from building in Lahore
Article Text:
LeT terrorist Chaudhary Muhammed Sarwar.

NEW DELHI: US designated Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Chaudhry Mohammad Sarwar alias Abu Hashim, one of the founding members of the outfit, died after mysteriously falling from the fourth floor of Markaz Qudesia in Lahore Sunday.The incident reminded of a similar death that had occurred in 2016 when fake currency kingpin, Javed Khanani, had died after falling from an under construction building in Karachi.Sarwar was currently handling the finance wing and fundraising excercise in Punjab province under the garb of the outfit's political wing, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League. He was a close aide of both Hafiz Saeed and current deputy chief Saifullah Kasuri. Sarwar's son had also died in a road accident a few months ago.It was in 2016 tha Sarwar was designated a terrorist by the US justice department who termed himself as a senior LeT memeber in Lahore active since early 2000s, holding various leadership roles in the group. At the time, he was LeT’s emir for Lahore, a position he has held since at least January 2015."As the LeT emir of Lahore, Sarwar maintains relationships with LeT’s most senior leaders. Between 2012 and 2013, Sarwar worked with LeT’s foreign affairs chief Hafiz Abdul Rahman Makki, and in early 2013, Makki asked Sarwar for money to pay for his travel within Pakistan," the US justice department had said in its statement."Sarwar had been directly involved in LeT fundraising activities and used the formal financial system in Pakistan to raise and move funds on behalf of LeT. For example, in 2008, Sarwar led delegations of businessmen to LeT facilities for the purpose of soliciting donations for the group," it added.
Article Summary: US designated Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Chaudhry Mohammad Sarwar alias Abu Hashim died after mysteriously falling from the fourth floor of Markaz Qudesia in Lahore Sunday. Sarwar was currently handling the finance wing and fundraising excercise in Punjab province under the garb of the outfit's political wing, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League.

Article Title: Pakistani forces kill 8 militants in Balochistan, raid hideouts as abductions rise
Article Text:
The operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas (Photo: ANI).

Pakistani security forces on Sunday reportedly killed eight militants in three intelligence-led operations across districts of Balochistan province, amid rising cases of abduction in the troubled region.The operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas, according to the Inter Service Public Relations (ISPR), the media wing of the Pakistan Army.In the Panjpai area of Quetta district, terrorists trying to set up a roadblock to disrupt local traffic were "intercepted by security forces, resulting in [the] killing of five terrorists", the ISPR said in a statement.In Nushki district, security forces stormed a hideout, and two terrorists were killed in an intense exchange of fire, the army said. Around 500 kilograms of explosives were also recovered from the terrorists during that operation. In Khuzdar district, one terrorist was killed, the ISPR added.Balochistan, which borders Afghanistan, has seen a surge in abductions and attacks on civilians and securityforces in recent years, prompting the government to step up its anti-militant operations.On Saturday, unidentified armed men hijacked a bus carrying 20 trainee police officers near Mastung, on the Quetta-Karachi highway, and took them away. Their whereabouts remain unknown.On Sunday, at least 18 workers were abducted, and another was injured when unidentified armed men attacked a marble mining site in the province. The incident happened early in the morning in the remote Naal area of Khuzdar district, police said. The attackers arrived on motorcycles and other vehicles and stormed the site.According to PTI, no insurgent group or individual has claimed responsibility for the attack.The police and the provincial government have yet to confirm the incident officially, but two police officers, speaking on condition of anonymity, said 18 workers had been taken away by the attackers. PTI reported."They came on bikes and vehicles and opened fire and then rounded up the workers present at the site and abducted 18 of them before fleeing," a police officer said.Most of those abducted came from nearby villages and areas, he added, and another worker was injured in the attack.
Article Summary: Pakistani security forces reportedly kill eight militants in three intelligence- led operations across districts of Balochistan province. Operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas. On Saturday, unidentified armed men hijacked a bus carrying 20 trainee police officers.

Article Title: Pakistan’s decades of backing terror comes full circle as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa falls under emergency rule
Article Text:
The emergency has also raised concerns about the separation of powers. In the affected districts, the constitutional distinction between judicial and executive authority has reportedly been set aside, concentrating control in unelected hands.

Decades of militant policy and blowback

Emergency rule and the erosion of elected authority

Opposition crackdown deepens rights concerns

Tribal communities face renewed uncertainty

Pakistan’s imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11 has placed the province under direct federal control. It has effectively suspended the regional administration led by imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).The move, which invokes Articles 232 and 234 of the Pakistani Constitution, comes amid a worsening security situation and a crackdown on opposition leaders and protesters. It has also renewed questions over Pakistan’s decades-long policy of using militant groups for strategic gains. A report by news agency ANI highlights how this policy has fuelled the violence now threatening its own territory.The emergency has extended federal control across 12 districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, further weakening elected authority in a province that has long borne the consequences of Pakistan’s security policies. The move follows years of political turmoil, including Khan’s imprisonment, constitutional amendments that have weakened judicial independence, and the removal of the PTI-led provincial government.The concentration of power in unelected authorities, alongside the military’s expanding role in civilian affairs, has raised concerns over the state of democracy in Pakistan, according to a report by news agency ANI.Pakistan’s security crisis has deep roots in its long-standing use of militant groups as instruments of state policy. For more than five decades, the country has pursued strategic depth through its relationship with armed groups, while distinguishing between factions considered useful and those viewed as threats.This approach has contributed to a cycle of violence that has increasingly turned inward.As stated in the report, the state has repeatedly shifted its position towards militant organisations, including groups hostile to its own security forces. During former army chief General Qamar Javed Bajwa’s tenure, cadres of the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) were relocated to parts of the erstwhile Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.The consequences have proved difficult to contain. Pakistan’s struggle with militancy has exposed the risks of treating armed groups as strategic assets while assuming their violence can be directed towards selected targets.Former US secretary of state Hillary Clinton captured this danger in a widely cited remark, “one cannot rear snakes in a backyard and expect them to bite only neighbours, as they will eventually turn on their keepers”.Rather than confronting the broader implications of this policy, Pakistan has continued to differentiate between militant factions it considers acceptable and those it seeks to eliminate. The resulting security failures have placed civilians, particularly in the tribal areas, at the centre of a prolonged conflict.The imposition of emergency rule marks another stage in the concentration of power within Pakistan’s security establishment. The federal intervention has effectively displaced the PTI-led provincial administration, depriving the opposition of its remaining provincial government.The move follows Khan’s incarceration and constitutional changes that have curtailed judicial independence and shielded military leadership from accountability. Critics argue that these developments have weakened the institutions meant to limit executive and military power.The emergency has also raised concerns about the separation of powers. In the affected districts, the constitutional distinction between judicial and executive authority has reportedly been set aside, concentrating control in unelected hands.Instead of addressing the failures behind the province’s deteriorating security situation, authorities have expanded federal and military involvement in civilian administration. The move has intensified concerns that emergency powers are being used not only to manage the security crisis but also to consolidate political control.The intervention has been accompanied by a wider crackdown on the opposition. Leaders and legislators have been detained, residences raided and political demonstrations suppressed. Protesters have faced police firing, tear gas and mass arrests.The treatment of political opponents has fuelled concerns that dissent is increasingly being treated as a security threat. The use of force against protesters has also raised questions about the government’s claim that extraordinary measures are needed to restore law and order.The crackdown comes amid concerns over restrictions on reporting from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, following earlier developments in Khyber before a blanket media ban was imposed on events in the province. Such restrictions risk limiting public scrutiny of security operations and their impact on civilians.The growing concentration of authority has therefore created a parallel crisis. While the state faces a persistent militant threat, its response has further narrowed the space for political opposition and public dissent.The latest intervention has also placed additional pressure on communities that have endured years of displacement and insecurity. Past military operations, including Zarb-e-Azb and Radd-ul-Fasad, remain associated with civilian hardship and human rights concerns.Thousands of displaced families are still awaiting return and rehabilitation. For these communities, the emergency raises fears of another period of disruption, particularly as the authorities expand their control and military involvement in civilian affairs.The consequences of Pakistan’s security policies have thus extended beyond the fight against armed groups. Tribal populations have faced displacement, civilian casualties and prolonged instability, while the failure to resolve the underlying conflict has left many vulnerable to further intervention.The emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa brings these tensions into sharper focus. A state that has long relied on militant groups to pursue strategic objectives now faces the consequences of violence within its own borders. Its response, however, has centred on expanding federal control, weakening elected authority and restricting opposition activity.Rather than resolving the crisis, the latest measures risk deepening the divide between the state and the communities it claims to protect. The removal of an elected provincial government, the concentration of power in unelected institutions and the crackdown on dissent point to a broader struggle over Pakistan’s democratic future, even as the country confronts the long-term fallout of its militant policies.
Article Summary: Emergency has extended federal control across 12 districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It has effectively suspended the regional administration led by Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) It comes amid a worsening security situation and a crackdown on opposition leaders and protesters. The emergency has also raised concerns about the separation of powers.

Article Title: Pakistan plans Moon landing by 2035, expands space cooperation with China
Article Text:
Pakistan sets 2035 Moon landing target as space programme expands, minister says (representative image)

First Pakistani astronaut to travel to China’s space station

Pakistan-China cooperation extends to lunar exploration

Space education and proposed museum

India’s space roadmap: From Gaganyaan to a Moon landing

Pakistan aims to land on the Moon by 2035 as it expands its space programme, planning minister Ahsan Iqbal said on Sunday, announcing that the country's first astronaut would embark on a space mission from China on November 25.Addressing the concluding ceremony of World Space Week 2026 in Narowal district of Punjab province, Iqbal said cooperation with China would help Pakistan advance its space exploration ambitions.Pakistan’s “first astronaut will embark on a space mission from China’s space centre on November 25, while the country aims to achieve a lunar landing by 2035,” he said, according to news agency PTI.The minister highlighted the growing role of space technology in agriculture, communications, climate monitoring, education and national security. He stressed that scientific research and space exploration were important for technological advancement.The upcoming mission is part of wider cooperation between Pakistan and China in space science and technology. According to Reuters, two Pakistani candidates, pilots Khurram Daud and Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, have been undergoing training in China, with one expected to be selected for the flight.The selected astronaut will serve as a payload specialist aboard China's Tiangong space station, conducting scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft, Reuters reported last month.Pakistan's space agency, the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO), signed an agreement with the China Manned Space Agency in February 2025 to prepare a Pakistani astronaut for the mission, according to The Express Tribune.The two candidates had been training at the China Astronaut Research and Training Centre in Beijing, learning spacecraft systems, Mandarin and the physical demands of spaceflight.The mission is expected to last about a week. The astronaut will travel aboard a Chinese spacecraft launched from China and return to Earth with members of a Chinese crew.Pakistan does not have an independent launch vehicle or crewed spacecraft, making the mission dependent on China's space infrastructure and training facilities.Beyond the human spaceflight programme, Pakistan and China are collaborating on a Pakistani-built lunar rover planned for China's Chang'e-8 mission, expected around 2028.The rover is intended to use artificial intelligence-based stereo imaging to identify obstacles, assess distances and navigate the lunar surface autonomously, as direct real-time control from Earth would not be possible.However, Pakistan's participation in the lunar rover project is separate from its stated ambition to land on the Moon by 2035.According to Reuters, a Pakistani space agency official last month had said there was no official commitment or discussion about sending a Pakistani astronaut to the Moon under the existing partnership.Iqbal was speaking at the conclusion of World Space Week 2026, which was celebrated in Narowal for the first time in collaboration with SUPARCO. The event aimed to raise awareness among young people about space science, scientific research and modern technology.The minister also announced plans to establish Pakistan's first Space Museum at the University of Narowal to promote scientific awareness and encourage students to pursue careers in space science and technology.He said improved access to higher education was allowing students who had previously faced financial barriers to perform well academically.Iqbal congratulated the University of Narowal on securing first position at the Islamabad Science Festival, saying the achievement reflected the talent and potential of Pakistan's youth.The minister said the proposed museum would further encourage young people to explore scientific fields and pursue opportunities in space research and technology.India has also been advancing its space programme, with plans to send astronauts into orbit, establish its own space station and land an Indian on the Moon by 2040.According to the Union government’s roadmap outlined in Parliament in August, the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission, carrying the humanoid robot Vyommitra, is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026. Two further uncrewed missions are planned before India attempts its first crewed orbital flight, targeted by 2027.India also plans to establish the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035. The proposed station will comprise five modules, with the development and launch of its first module already approved.The longer-term goal is to send an Indian astronaut to the Moon by 2040.Other planned missions include Chandrayaan-4, which is intended to demonstrate technologies for returning lunar samples to Earth, and a Venus Orbiter Mission to study the planet’s surface, subsurface and atmosphere.These projects form part of India’s broader Space Vision 2047, which aims to expand its human spaceflight capabilities and deepen its role in space exploration.
Article Summary: Pakistan's first astronaut will embark on a space mission from China on November 25. Ahsan Iqbal said cooperation with China would help Pakistan advance its space exploration ambitions. Pakistan and China are collaborating on a Pakistani-built lunar rover planned for China's Chang'e-8 mission, expected around 2028.

Article Title: Balochistan unrest: Teacher's killing sparks outrage, kin say Pak officials shielding 'death squads'
Article Text:
What are Balochistan's 'death squads'?

(With ANI inputs)

The alleged torture and killing of a teacher in Pakistan’s restive Balochistan province triggered protests by his family members and local residents, who warned that a key highway would be blockaded if authorities failed to take action.The protesters accused Pakistani forces of shielding those allegedly responsible for the death of Parvez Mazar, an Arabic teacher at Government High School Babbar Shor in Pasni, a coastal town in Balochistan’s Gwadar district, The Balochistan Post reported.According to Mazar’s relatives, he was "taken away" in front of his family on Tuesday and was found dead the following day. They claimed that members of a state-backed armed group, described as a “death squad,” took him to a private torture facility, where he was detained and killed.Protesters, including Mazar’s children, gathered outside the Pasni Press Club, demanding the immediate arrest of those responsible for his death. They demanded accountability and justice for the deceased teacher's family.The demonstrators warned that failure to address their demands would prompt them to stage a sit-in at Pasni Zero Point and block the Makran Coastal Highway, a key route connecting Gwadar with Karachi in Sindh province, Pakistan’s largest city and the country's financial and commercial hub.They demanded that state institutions take action against armed groups accused of abducting, torturing and killing civilians while allegedly operating under the protection of state agencies.Baloch rights organisations and activists use the term “death squads” to describe armed groups they allege receive support or protection from Pakistani state institutions.These groups have been accused of targeting civilians, political activists and human rights defenders in Balochistan, a province long affected by an insurgency and a security crackdown.
Article Summary: Pervez Mazar, an Arabic teacher at Government High School Babbar Shor in Pasni, a coastal town in Balochistan’s Gwadar district, was found dead the following day. His family claimed that members of a state-backed armed group, described as a “death squad,” took him to a private torture facility, where he was detained and killed.

Article Title: Strong 6.0-magnitude quake strikes Balochistan in Pakistan
Article Text:
6.0-magnitude quake strikes Balochistan in Pakistan

More details awaited

An earthquake measuring 6.0 in magnitude struck southern Pakistan near Khuzdar, Balochistan on Saturday, around 95 km south of Sūrāb, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC).The German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said the earthquake struck at a depth of 10 km (6 miles).
Article Summary: An earthquake measuring 6.0 in magnitude struck southern Pakistan near Khuzdar, Balochistan on Saturday. The German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said the earthquake struck at a depth of 10 km (6 miles)

Article Title: Imran Khan facing Nawaz, Benazir-style exile deal? Pakistan opposition leader's big claim
Article Text:
Imran Khan

What happened in Nawaz Sharif, Benazir Bhutto's exile cases?

Achakzai demands access to prisoners, empowered parliament

Opposition challenges governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

Pakistan opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai has claimed that jailed former prime minister Imran Khan is being pressured into an agreement similar to arrangements that led former premiers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto into exile, according to a report by Dawn published on Saturday.Achakzai, chairman of the Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) and leader of the opposition in Pakistan's National Assembly, made the claim at a news conference at the Peshawar high court on Friday. He alleged that the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) were involved in a similar political arrangement.“The same is happening today with the PML-N and PPP in government,” Achakzai said, according to Dawn.The claim comes amid political tensions surrounding Imran Khan, founder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), who remains in prison, and opposition allegations over restrictions on political activity and the functioning of elected institutions.Achakzai was accompanied by Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) leaders Sardar Akhtar Mengal and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas. He said opposition parties were in contact and that a multi-party conference would be convened soon.He also said resigning from the assemblies remained an option, adding that the opposition had submitted its demands in response to an offer of negotiations.Achakzai's remarks referred to the circumstances in which Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto, two of Pakistan's most prominent former prime ministers, spent periods outside the country following political upheavals, Dawnreported.Sharif was ousted and imprisoned after a military coup led by then-army chief Pervez Musharraf. He left Pakistan in 2000 under a deal negotiated with the involvement of Saudi and Lebanese leaders.Bhutto, meanwhile, went into self-imposed exile after her Pakistan Peoples Party lost the 1997 general elections, following her dismissal by then-president Farooq Leghari. Her husband, Asif Ali Zardari, was imprisoned on corruption charges and was released in 2004.Achakzai's comparison suggests that he believes a similar arrangement could be pursued in Khan's case. However, his remarks, as reported by Dawn, did not establish that an exile agreement involving the PTI founder had been reached.During the news conference, Achakzai criticised restrictions on prisoners' access to meetings and called for changes to what he described as a "wrong amendment". He also demanded that parliament be empowered and an independent commission be established to ensure transparent elections.“Nowhere in the world is a prisoner denied meetings,” he said, according to Dawn.He argued that political disputes could not be resolved without strengthening parliament. He also expressed concern over the whereabouts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's chief minister and other lawmakers, demanding that the authorities disclose the chief minister's location.“We stand with the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The people of this province have the first right over its minerals. Regardless of political affiliation, everyone must unite for the homeland,” he said, adding that they would be safer if the country survived.Mengal, who accompanied Achakzai, criticised the government's actions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and questioned the imposition of governor's rule on grounds of terrorism. He also alleged that elected representatives had been displaced and questioned the legitimacy of the political system.Raja Nasir Abbas, the opposition leader in the Senate, also criticised the situation, saying: “You cannot run a country, yet you have occupied a province,” according to Dawn.Separately, TTAP leaders approached the Peshawar High Court on Friday, challenging the proclamation of emergency and the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.According to Dawn, the petitioners asked the court to declare the October 11 proclamation, issued under Articles 232(1) and 234 of Pakistan's Constitution, unconstitutional and without lawful authority. They argued that the constitutional conditions required for imposing the measures had not been met or that the government had exceeded its powers.The petition also challenged the purported transfer of the provincial assembly's legislative powers to parliament, the displacement of the elected chief minister and provincial cabinet, and the establishment of the proposed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Advisory Council and Area Development Secretariat.The petitioners sought the annulment of executive orders and notifications linked to the proclamation, including the deployment of armed forces to the extent that it allegedly violated constitutional requirements.They also requested interim relief to prevent the displacement of elected institutions and restrictions on elected representatives while the court considers the case.The legal challenge adds to the opposition's broader campaign against federal intervention in the province, as Achakzai seeks to bring opposition parties together over constitutional issues, political rights and negotiations with the government.
Article Summary: Mahmood Khan Achakzai claims Imran Khan is being pressured into an agreement similar to those that led Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto into exile. He claims the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) are involved in a similar political arrangement. The opposition leader made the claim at a news conference at the Peshawar high court on Friday.

Article Title: Pakistan to chair IMF, World Bank boards in 2027; first time in over 70 years
Article Text:
The announcement was made during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok (Photo: AP).

Pakistan will take over the chairmanship of the boards of governors of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in 2027, returning to the position for the first time since 1953, the country’s ministry of economic affairs said on Friday.The announcement was made during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok, where Pakistan’s minister for economic affairs Ahad Khan Cheema, who also serves as the country’s governor to the World Bank, was formally designated as the incoming chair, PTI reported.Describing the appointment as a “historic milestone”, the ministry said the role would allow Pakistan to participate in shaping global economic and development discussions and encourage constructive engagement among member countries.The annual meetings, scheduled from October 12 to 18, have brought together more than 15,000 participants representing 191 countries.The appointment comes as Pakistan continues to rely on financial assistance from the IMF through two programmes: a USD 7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a USD 1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).While the EFF is aimed at meeting the country’s balance-of-payments needs and supporting economic reforms, the RSF provides longer-term funding to help Pakistan tackle climate-related risks and improve its resilience.Pakistan could receive a further USD 1.2 billion from the IMF, subject to approval by the fund’s Executive Board. The anticipated disbursement follows an agreement reached between IMF staff and Pakistani authorities on the latest reviews of both programmes.
Article Summary: Pakistan will take over the chairmanship of the boards of governors of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in 2027. The announcement was made during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF annual meetings in Bangkok. Pakistan continues to rely on financial assistance from the IMF through two programmes.

Article Title: Pakistan ranks lowest in South Asia on hunger index amid rising food prices
Article Text:
Pakistan's 2026 Global Hunger Index standings reveal an alarming crisis, showcasing the worst performance in South Asia amid ongoing economic challenges. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Economic crisis and food inflation worsen Pakistan’s hunger situation

Hunger reduction stalls across South Asia

Extreme weather threatens regional food production

Millions across South Asia continue to face undernourishment

Pakistan has recorded the poorest performance in South Asia in the 2026 global hunger index (GHI), reflecting mounting food insecurity driven by economic instability, rising food prices, climate-related disasters and international conflicts, according to a report by Dawn.Titled “No Security Without Food Security”, the report was jointly prepared by German aid organisation Welthungerhilfe, the institute for international law of peace and armed conflict at Ruhr university Bochum, and swiss organisation helvetas.According to the news agency ANI, the findings indicate that progress in reducing hunger across South Asia has largely stagnated, while Pakistan and Afghanistan have experienced a deterioration in conditions since 2018.Pakistan’s economic challenges and persistent food inflation have eroded household purchasing power, making it increasingly difficult for families to access sufficient and nutritious food.The report noted that Pakistan’s undernourishment indicator had deteriorated from a low level in 2018 to a medium level. Meanwhile, child wasting has approached the threshold associated with the high category, underscoring continuing concerns over child nutrition.South Asia recorded an overall global hunger index score of 23.5, placing the region in the serious category. While the score represents an improvement from 37.5 in 2000, the report suggests that much of the progress was achieved before 2018.Over the past two decades, Pakistan and Afghanistan have moved out of the alarming hunger category. However, persistent levels of child malnutrition continue to pose a significant challenge in both countries.Child stunting has continued to decline in Pakistan, while Afghanistan has recorded a slight increase in the indicator since 2018.Child mortality rates have improved in both countries, falling from very high levels in 2000 to medium levels in the latest assessment.The report also drew attention to the growing impact of extreme weather events on agricultural production and food security across South Asia.Heavy rainfall and flooding damaged crops in parts of Pakistan and Bangladesh. In Afghanistan, inadequate rainfall and unusually high temperatures disrupted the cereal-growing season in 2026.These climate-related pressures could further aggravate food shortages and prolong acute food insecurity across the region, according to Dawn.Estimates from the food and agriculture organisation (FAO) indicate that approximately 218 million people across South Asia, including Iran, experienced undernourishment between 2023 and 2025.This represents roughly one-third of the global population affected by undernourishment during the period, highlighting the scale of the region’s food security challenge.The findings underscore the need for sustained efforts to address economic vulnerabilities, improve access to nutritious food and strengthen agricultural resilience against climate-related shocks.
Article Summary: Pakistan has recorded the poorest performance in South Asia in the 2026 global hunger index (GHI) The report was prepared by German aid organisation Welthungerhilfe, the institute for international law of peace and armed conflict at Ruhr university Bochum, and swiss organisation helvetas. The findings indicate that progress in reducing hunger across South Asia has largely stagnated.

Article Title: 33 children, teacher killed as school roof collapses in Pakistan’s Peshawar
Article Text:
18 killed as school roof collapses in Pakistan's Peshawar

At least 33 students and a teacher were killed after the roof of a school collapsed in Pakistan 's Peshawar city on Thursday.Twenty students and a female teacher were killed and more than 40 people injured in the incident, officials said.Peshawar Capital City Police chief Mian Saeed said the incident occurred in Dir Colony in the city's inner area, as cited by PTI.Lady Reading Hospital spokesperson Muhammad Asim said an emergency had been declared at the facility to treat the injured.All the children killed in the incident were aged 13 or younger, Asim said. Rescue officials said 25 injured children had been taken to medical facilities.Rescue teams were clearing the debris and searching for children and school staff who might still be trapped beneath the collapsed structure.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep grief over the loss of life and extended his condolences to the bereaved families.Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, largely due to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials.In July, three girls aged between three and 13 were killed when part of the outer wall of a government primary school near Umerkot collapsed, burying them under the debris, as cited by Dawn.That same month, a child was killed and at least five others were injured when the roof of an under-construction private school building collapsed in Lahore’s Baghbanpura neighbourhood.In June, 14 children died after the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. Less than two months earlier, four children were killed and 20 people injured when a classroom roof collapsed at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan.
Article Summary: Twenty students and a female teacher were killed and more than 40 people injured in the incident. The incident occurred in Dir Colony in the city's inner area. Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep grief over the loss of life and extended his condolences to the bereaved families.

Article Title: Pakistan regulator warns TV channels against live coverage of blasts and terror attacks
Article Text:
The regulator also stressed the need for stronger editorial oversight.

Channels told to air only verified information

Legal action for violations

Pakistan's media regulator has warned satellite television channels against broadcasting live footage of explosions, gunfire and terrorist attacks, cautioning that violations could lead to legal action.The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) issued a notification on Tuesday, reminding broadcasters of restrictions first introduced on February 20, 2023. The rules bar news, current affairs and regional-language channels from broadcasting, rebroadcasting or providing live coverage of such incidents.The directive comes as emergency rule has been imposed in the north-western province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, renewing debate over how the media should report security incidents while ensuring that the public receives timely and reliable information.PEMRA has instructed broadcasters to air only “verified information warranted by the relevant government departments or law enforcement agencies”.The regulator also stressed the need for stronger editorial oversight and the effective use of broadcast delays to prevent the immediate transmission of sensitive footage during security incidents.It directed television channels to establish independent editorial boards in line with applicable laws and relevant court judgments.The notification referred to the Supreme Court's judgment in Suo Motu Case No. 28 of 2018 and an Islamabad High Court order dated September 5, 2022, both concerning the prescribed procedure for broadcast delays.PEMRA warned that channels violating the directive could face legal proceedings under Sections 29A, 30 and 33 of the PEMRA Ordinance, 2002, as amended.The latest notification reiterates the regulator's existing restrictions on live coverage of security incidents, with a focus on verification, editorial checks and the use of broadcast delays.
Article Summary: Pakistan's media regulator has warned satellite television channels against broadcasting live footage of explosions, gunfire and terrorist attacks. The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) issued a notification on Tuesday. The rules bar news, current affairs and regional-language channels from broadcasting or providing live coverage of such incidents.
